793.name: Outdoor adventurous activities: teamwork, fitness and movement skills
793.description: This unit explores skillful movement and physical fitness through teamwork challenges. Pupils will develop teamwork skills and understand both why and how to warm up for different types of physical activity.
793.why: At primary school, pupils are introduced to basic outdoor and adventurous activities (OAA), teamwork, and fitness challenges. This unit at the start of secondary school levels the playing field for those with less exposure to competitive sports and helps everyone feel they belong in PE. The OAA elements help pupils get familiar with their new environment and teamwork challenges encourage mixing beyond immediate friends. Later, pupils will face more complex physical and intellectual challenges in OAA.
prior: Pupils know they should warm up prior to participation in sport and physical activity.
Pupils understand the difference between physical and intellectual challenges.
Pupils are able to work in small groups to solve simple problems and achieve a set task.
Pupils show a creative approach to tackling problems with increasing confidence.

794.name: Invasion games: basic tactics to overcome opponents in donor sports
794.description: This unit explores tactics to overcome opponents with a focus on keeping possession of a ball either in hand or at your feet. Pupils will learn how to move on and off the ball to create space, to create options and to outwit others in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios that can be applied to many sports.
794.why: Pupils will already have explored basic principles of attack and defence and experimented with tactics and power plays. They will unpick why creating space is essential for success in invasion games and how to achieve this as a team with deception, creativity and the use of set plays. The importance of good positioning and a strong stance is explored both when shooting and defending. The unit will take an overarching look at the basic tactics required to outwit opponents without focussing on a specific sport or activity.
prior: Pupils know that all invasion games have similar features of attacking and defensive play to either score or deny scoring opportunities respectively.
Pupils understand that football, netball, rugby, basketball and handball are all examples of invasion games with different rules but all games are played as a team.
Pupils are able to control and pass a ball in a variety of ways.
Pupils show a willingness to try new activities and focus on improving their skills.
threads: Move: application of tactics, strategies and compositional ideas

795.name: Invasion games: basic tactics to overcome opponents through futsal
795.description: This unit will build on fundamental skills and apply tactics to overcome opponents through futsal. Development of basic ball control, passing, shooting, dribbling, marking and tackling skills with determination in small sided games. Pupils will learn the rules of futsal and names of major muscles.
795.why: Pupils will already have explored principles of keeping possession of a ball either in hand or at feet in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios (core tasks). Pupils will now apply that learning to move on and off the ball to create space, to create options and to outwit others in futsal. The heavier ball lends itself to small sided games, increased control and keeping the ball on the floor to support less experienced pupils and level the playing field. Later in invasion games they will also apply these principles to netball.
prior: Pupils know that all invasion games involve elements of attacking and defending to either score or deny scoring opportunities.
Pupils understand how to apply basic attacking and defensive principles in a game situation.
Pupils are able to create space with their movement off the ball to increase scoring opportunities.
Pupils show the ability to work effectively as a team, applying basic tactics in small sided games.
threads: Think: knowledge of rules, tactics, strategies and compositional ideas

796.name: Gymnastics: body control and paired sequences
796.description: This unit will explore core gymnastics skills both individually and in combination. Pupils will develop their stability whilst holding their own body position and when supporting a partner. They will learn how to give appropriate feedback to others on posture and the execution of short sequences.
796.why: Pupils will already have experienced basic ideas in gymnastics to include exploring how to balance, roll, rotate and safe ways to land from apparatus including a bench. Pupils will now refine their technique and body awareness to execute more challenging skills and build more complex sequences in pairs. Later in gymnastics they will become more technically fluent and able to analyse group performances.
prior: Pupils know that gymnastics requires good body control and an awareness of safety to always work within personal capabilities.
Pupils understand that gymnastics requires the development of individual skills but also collaborative skills to support each other to refine and improve their performance.
Pupils are able to perform basic balances and create a short sequence with good body form.
Pupils show an awareness of each other and appreciate that some balances, rotations or vaults will be more familiar to some pupils than others.

797.name: Net and wall games: maintain and win a rally through pickleball
797.description: This unit will explore basic skills to start, maintain and win a rally in racket sports. Pupils will learn the specific rules to pickleball and develop persistence when improving racket skills to play in pairs. They will also work on observation skills to officiate and improve performance.
797.why: Pupils will already have explored basic bat and ball (net/ wall) games at primary school. This requires pupils to transfer and apply previously learnt principles of attack and defence to consider how they apply in a different context. They will need to persist with tasks set and develop their ability to observe others to officiate and/ or coach. Later in net and wall games they will develop basic skills and hand-eye coordination further whilst also learning specific rules and techniques for badminton and tennis.
prior: Pupils know the basic format for racket sports to include terms like serve, forehand, backhand, singles and doubles.
Pupils understand why they have to aim at space in order to beat an opponent.
Pupils are able to create a short cooperative rally with their partner.
Pupils show an ability to manage their emotions and focus on skills to improve their technique/performance.

798.name: Invasion games: basic tactics to overcome opponents through netball
798.description: This unit will build on fundamental skills and apply tactics to overcome opponents through netball. Development of basic passing, receiving, footwork, dodging, shooting, and defending skills with positivity in small sided games. Pupils will learn the rules of netball and names of major bones.
798.why: Pupils will already have explored principles of keeping possession of a ball either in hand or at feet in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios (core tasks). Pupils will now apply that learning to pass accurately and move off the ball to create space and options to outwit others in netball. They will improve their quality of movement to avoid breaking the footwork rule and also refine skills to accurately replicate the shooting technique via reciprocal learning. Later in invasion games they will experience basketball.
prior: Pupils know that all invasion games have similar features of attacking and defending play to either score or deny scoring opportunities.
Pupils understand that netball is an invasion game.
Pupils are able to throw and catch a ball in a variety of ways.
Pupils show a willingness to try new activities and focus on improving their skills.
threads: Think: decision making, problem solving and creative thinking

800.name: Dance: identity
800.description: This unit is a thematic approach drawing upon personal experiences to consolidate and deepen their knowledge and understanding of Action-Space-Dynamics-Relationships to create, develop and analyse ideas, motifs and dances. They will use similarities and differences to form connections and contrast.
800.why: Throughout KS1 and 2, pupils have had the opportunity to choreograph dance sequences in character, demonstrating musicality, emotion and creativity, aligned to multiple stimuli. This unit will take the next step into developing pupils' knowledge and application of specific dance steps and challenge pupils to focus on the aesthetics of their performance as opposed to characterisation. Pupils will be required to utilise all of their knowledge and understanding around choreography, to create and perform complex dance sequences using specific dance steps with accurate timings.
prior: Pupils can use dance as an effective means of communicating ideas.
Pupils can refine the communication of an idea by applying space, dynamics, relationships or stylistic features.
Pupils can use a variety of techniques to respond to a stimuli.
Pupils can vary or develop motifs and use them effectively to build short dances alone or in a group.
Pupils can utilise a wide range of physical, choreographic and analytical skills concurrently.

801.name: Striking and fielding games: bowling, batting and fielding with accuracy
801.description: This unit will develop core skills in batting, bowling and fielding with the intention of outwitting opponents. Pupils will learn to play simple games with a variety of equipment to ensure success and be given quality practice time to focus on accuracy in games like rounders.
801.why: Pupils will already have explored basic skills of batting and running to score as well as bowling and fielding to deny scoring opportunities through an introduction to rounders and cricket. Pupils will now refine these skills to improve accuracy and become increasingly aware of the impact of misfielding. Later in striking and fielding games pupils will apply principles to cricket and learn to compete and to analyse performance to suggest ways to improve.
prior: Pupils know how to play a range of positions demonstrating a variety of skills including throwing, catching and striking the ball.
Pupils understand the basic rules associated with scoring runs and getting players out involved in different striking and fielding games.
Pupils are able to apply basic tactics when batting to hit away from fielders and to avoid a mis-field when retrieving a long ball.
Pupils show the ability to communicate effectively as a team when making a decision on running and where to field a ball in to.

802.name: Athletics: run, jump, throw and officiate
802.description: This unit will explore core techniques and use knowledge to become more technically proficient at sprinting, jogging and a range of both jumping and throwing events. Pupils will learn how the body responds to different types of exercise, how to be self-motivated and how to officiate fairly.
802.why: Pupils will already have experienced a range of athletics events and have some awareness of the differences between sprinting fast and pacing yourself for running longer distances. They will have experimented with jumping for height, jumping for distance and ways to throw different implements such as tennis balls, quoits and foam/ vortex javelins. Later in athletics they will train and refine skills further whilst also learning to operate as a mini-team through a sport education season.
prior: Pupils know that athletic performances require maximal effort.
Pupils understand that running over different distances requires different speeds and techniques.
Pupils are able to perform throwing actions with effective starting position and transfer of weight.
Pupils show perseverance when competing at their personal best level.

1811.name: Remote learning: games making
1811.description: This unit will explore basic agility, balance and coordination skills with a focus on ball control and challenges to develop competence in a range of games. Pupils will need to think creatively to modify the ideas presented to them whilst producing personal best performances.
1811.why: Pupils will already have experienced simple target games and understand basic principles of attack and defence. They will explore ways to control and manipulate a ball with their hands and/or feet, whilst setting increasing complex challenges to accomplish and also design games that provide an immersive experience to practice their ball handling skills.
prior: Pupils know that all games have similar features of attacking and defensive play to either score or deny scoring opportunities respectively.
Pupils understand that football, netball, rugby, basketball and handball are all examples of invasion games with different rules.
Pupils are able to control and pass a ball in a variety of ways.
Pupils show a willingness to try new activities and focus on improving their skills.

1812.name: Remote learning: moving with confidence
1812.description: This unit will support the development of quality movement by focusing on form, body control and foundational movement skills such as agility, balance and coordination. Pupils will be challenged to accurately replicate an increasingly complex variety of movements with control and fluency.
1812.why: Pupils will already have experienced basic movement tasks to include exploring how to balance, rotate and safe ways to land. Pupils will now refine their technique and body awareness to execute more challenging skills and build more complex sequences of movement.
prior: Pupils know that good body control and an awareness of safety is essential and includes always working within personal capabilities.
Pupils understand that improving individual skills requires focus and dedication to practice.
Pupils are able to perform basic forms of locomotion and balances with good body form.
Pupils show an awareness of the dedication and hours required to see significant improvements in movement quality, control and fluency.

1813.name: Remote learning: dance development
1813.description: This unit focuses upon personal experiences to consolidate and deepen pupil knowledge and understanding of Action-Space-Dynamics-Relationships to create, develop and analyse ideas, motifs and dances. Pupils will use similarities and differences to form connections and contrast.
1813.why: Throughout KS1 and KS2, pupils have had the opportunity to choreograph dance sequences in character, demonstrating musicality, emotion and creativity, aligned to multiple stimuli. This unit will take the next step into developing pupils' knowledge and application of specific dance steps and challenge pupils to focus on the aesthetics of their performance. Pupils will be required to utilise their current knowledge and understanding around choreography in order to create and perform complex dance sequences, using specific dance steps alongside accurate timing.
prior: Pupils know how to use dance as an effective means of communicating ideas.
Pupils understand a variety of techniques to respond to a stimuli.
Pupils are able to develop motifs and use them effectively to build short dance routines.
Pupils show an awareness of a wide range of physical, choreographic and analytical skills concurrently.

1814.name: Remote learning: outdoor adventure activities
1814.description: This unit will enhance pupils' ability to respond effectively to physical challenges and problems. A key focus will be on developing planning and strategic thinking by requiring pupils to methodically solve problems under time constraints. Pupils will develop critical reflection skills.
1814.why: Pupils will already have developed basic skills to operate as a team but this unit challenges pupils to apply them in unique scenarios that require problem solving and creative thinking. Later in outdoor adventurous activities, pupils will get the opportunity to engage in activities beyond the school walls which will further develop their teamwork and leadership skills.
prior: Pupils know the importance of using logical and creative thinking to solve problems.
Pupils understand that in order to improve, we need to reflect on both the positives and negatives of our performance.
Pupils are able to work under pressure, often against the clock.
Pupils show patience and resilience when faced with a challenging task.

1815.name: Remote learning: health and fitness
1815.description: This unit explores correct bodyweight techniques and training for strength, power, endurance, flexibility, balance and coordination. Pupils learn to adapt exercises, stay safe and understand the physical, mental and social benefits of activity.
1815.why: Pupils will already have experienced elements of fitness training and have improved their understanding of how the body responds to exercise. Later in health and wellbeing, pupils will learn more about setting SMART targets to help motivate and review progress.
prior: Pupils know that taking part in fitness activities can have a positive impact on their health.
Pupils understand that different people have different fitness levels.
Pupils are able to perform basic exercises to improve fitness such as running or bodyweight exercises.
Pupils show ways to adapt exercise to suit their needs and motivations.

804.name: Inclusive sports: teamship, communication and awareness of others
804.description: This unit explores how to measure success beyond the outcomes of competition, how to balance competition, and how to ensure games are inclusive, respectful, supportive and engaging for all. Pupils will develop their teamship skills through improved communication, empathy and awareness of others.
804.why: Pupils will already have developed their foundational movement skills and ability to apply tactics to overcome opponents in a variety of invasion games. Being able to work with others in a respectful, kind and compassionate way is an important skill and forms the focus of this unit through a variety of contexts that help raise awareness. Later pupils will be expected to apply these skills in a broad range of games and other activities.
prior: Pupils know about the Paralympics and some of the inclusive sports that exist.
Pupils understand some of the skills required to be an effective leader.
Pupils can showan appreciation of etiquette.

805.name: Invasion games: tactics and strategies to outwit opponents in donor sports
805.description: This unit explores a wider range of tactics and strategies to include dispersal, penetration, support and screening in attack whilst defensive strategies of delay, compactness, depth, balance and control/ restraint can be applied in many sports with the ball in hand, at feet or on a stick.
805.why: Pupils will already have explored tactics to overcome opponents with a focus on keeping possession of a ball either in hand or at your feet. Pupils will have learnt how to move on and off the ball to create space, to create options and to outwit others in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios but also through transferring and applying these skills in specific sports like futsal and netball. They will increasingly show the emotional intelligence to work well with their peers. Later in invasion games they will apply these tactics and strategies in games like football and rugby.

Pupils understand how to beat defenders through movement with the ball, movement off the ball and passing.

806.name: Invasion games: tactics and strategies to outwit opponents through football
806.description: This unit will apply a wider range of tactics and strategies through football. Increasingly complex approaches to attack and strategies to defend will be applied whilst enhancing knowledge of the rules and tactics specific to football. Pupils will also work on their organisational skills.
806.why: Pupils will already have explored a wider range of tactics and strategies to include dispersal, penetration, support and screening in attack whilst defensive strategies of delay, compactness, depth, balance and control/ restraint in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios but also through futsal so now they can apply these to the specific sport of football. Later in invasion games and other competitions they will explore ways to outwit, using advanced tactics and strategies, full-contact sports like rugby.

807.name: Health and wellbeing: long term benefits of physical activity through circuits
807.description: This unit will explore the correct technique for body weight exercises along with an understanding of how to adapt and modify stations to ensure a training benefit. Pupils will learn about the physical, mental and social benefits of physical activity and how to ensure they are safe when training.
807.why: Pupils will already have experienced elements of fitness training and have improved their understanding of how the body responds to exercise through OAA: teamwork, fitness and movement skills in action as well as athletics: run, throw, jump and officiate. Later in health and wellbeing pupils will learn more about leadership and setting SMART targets to help motivate and review progress.
prior: Pupils know that taking part in fitness activities can have a positive impact on their health.
Pupils understand that different people have different fitness levels.
Pupils are able to perform basic exercises to improve fitness such as running or bodyweight exercises.
Pupils show ways to adapt exercise to suit their needs and motivations.

808.name: Gymnastics jigsaw: technical fluency and group performance analysis
808.description: This unit will explore the use of various apparatus and flight based sequences whilst also giving pupils the opportunity to master, teach each other and analyse group performances. They will also learn how to set out their space safely.
808.why: Pupils will already have experienced core gymnastics skills including balances, rotations, rolls and simple partner work. They will now improve their technical fluency, movement competence and awareness whilst also analysing group performances. Later they will explore rolling, flight and creative movement further through parkour and further develop their problem solving and analytical skills.
prior: Pupils know that high quality gymnastics requires good body awareness, balance and control.
Pupils understand how to work in larger groups to develop high quality routines.
Pupils are able to support one another to analyse and improve their gymnastics skills.
Pupils show a willingness to choreograph a routine incorporating a range of skills and a variety of balances individually, in pairs and as a group.

809.name: Net and wall games: technical proficiency and problem solving through badminton
809.description: This unit will apply hand-eye coordination and racket skills to badminton with a focus on problem solving to win points and increasing proficiency with serves, clears and smashes. Pupils will also develop their ability to analyse performances to identify strengths and weaknesses.
809.why: Pupils will already have explored basic skills to hit forehands and backhands and ideas for maintaining rallies in pickleball. This unit requires pupils to transfer these skills and basic tactics to badminton where every shot is hit without a bounce. They will need to accurately replicate key techniques whilst also figuring out how to outwit their opposition. Later in net and wall games they will understand more about effective performance and further develop their decision making skills.
prior: Pupils know from pickleball about lunging to move around court and serving from behind the baseline and alternating sides whilst continuing to serve if they win the point.
Pupils understand the difference between groundstrokes, volleys, drops, smashes and lobs as well as the importance of varying pace and angle to outwit their opponent.
Pupils are able to maintain a cooperative rally by hitting predominately to their partners forehand and can feed a ball for their partner to practice shots.
Pupils show an ability to persevere with tasks set and self-officiate games of singles and doubles fairly.

811.name: Invasion games: tactics and strategies to outwit through rugby
811.description: This unit will develop knowledge of the rules and apply a wider range of tactics and strategies through rugby. Pupils will apply attacking and defensive strategies with creativity and careful consideration of safety.
811.why: Pupils will already have explored a wider range of tactics and strategies to include dispersal, penetration, support and screening in attack whilst defensive strategies of delay, compactness, depth, balance and control/ restraint in ‘donor’ sports and scenarios but also through football so now they can transfer these (where appropriate) to the specific sport of rugby. Later in invasion games they will explore more ways to outwit in full-contact sports.

812.name: Dance: crossing continents
812.description: The unit explores a stylistic approach that outlines the different application of Action-Space-Dynamics-Relationships to four contrasting but inter-related dance styles enabling the learners to draw comparisons and consider why and how wider societal factors affected their evolution.
812.why: This unit develops pupils understanding of how we can learn about a society through the arts and how they reflect and affect the norms and accepted culture of their time. Pupils will be introduced to how the dance styles studied spread in terms of their geographic reach as well shifting between fulfilling a social function into an art form. This unit builds upon the work in the ‘Everyday Art’ unit, appreciating the purposes of art. Pupils will refine their sense of aesthetics, accuracy of placement and be able to identify key stylistic qualities.

Pupils can reflect upon the various functions of art and their evolution.
Pupils can synthesise a wide range of physical skills.
Pupils can identify a selection of methods regarding how they might develop a motif and justify their choices.

813.name: Outdoor adventurous activities: physical and intellectual challenges
813.description: This unit explores pupils' ability to respond effectively to problems and physical challenges, both individually and in cooperation with others. Developing awareness of others and ability to work in teams is essential to success in life and in this unit.
813.why: Pupils will already have developed basic skills to operate as a team but this unit challenges pupils to apply them in unique scenarios that require problem solving and creative thinking. Later in outdoor adventurous activities pupils will get the opportunity to engage in activities beyond the school walls, which will further develop their teamwork and leadership skills.
prior: Pupils know that basic fundamental movement skills form the building blocks for other physical movement skills.

Pupils are able to build and maintain trust when working in small groups.
Pupils show patience and resilience when faced with a challenging task.

814.name: Striking and fielding games: competition and performance analysis in cricket
814.description: This unit will develop techniques for batting in cricket whilst bringing in statistical analysis to help with decision making. Fielding skills will be refined before overarm bowling is refined to enable games of pairs cricket.
814.why: Pupils will already have explored the core skills of batting, bowling and fielding in an attempt to score or deny runs. The drive and pull shots will enable pupils to place the ball in different areas of the field before testing confidence, mental capacity and appetite for risk through small sided scoring and officiating games. Later in striking and fielding games pupils will play and officiate their own small sided team games of cricket and continue to develop their ability to analyse performances.

Pupils understand that although batting is an individual skill, it is part of a team performance and impacts others.
Pupils are able to perform different types of throws to suit the distance and situation.
Pupils show the ability to alter striking and fielding strategies in response to various factors and team dynamics.

815.name: Athletics: train and perform in a sport education season
815.description: This unit will develop pupils’ ability to perform in a range of athletic events with a focus on personal best improvements. They will learn about different components of fitness and the difference between aerobic and anaerobic exercise. Pupils will take responsibility for working in small teams.
815.why: Pupils will already have developed the necessary core techniques for different running, jumping and throwing events. After they train to improve different aspects of fitness, pupils will contribute towards the performance of their team as they grow in confidence and challenge themselves to improve further. Later in athletics pupils will focus on pace or power whilst demonstrating increasing independence.

Pupils understand that within teams, there are roles such as coach, performer, and official.

Pupils respond positively to feedback and are motivated to improve their personal best performances.

816.name: Invasion games: adapt tactics and strategies in contact sports
816.description: This unit explores ways to adapt tactics and strategies in full-contact sports like rugby. Pupils will learn how to respond to specific types of breakdown such as free kicks, rucks, mauls and scrums as they seek solutions to gain territory, maintain momentum and counterattack.
816.why: Pupils will already have explored a wider range of tactics and strategies to include dispersal, penetration, support and screening in attack whilst defensive strategies of delay, compactness, depth, balance and control/ restraint will have been applied in a range of scenarios and specific sports like football, netball and rugby. This unit takes that understanding into a variety of full-contact situations that require great teamwork and the confidence to engage in tackles/ full body contact. Pupils will also learn about sporting values and fair play, which is developed in many future units.

822.name: Invasion games: adapt tactics and strategies through handball
822.description: This unit explores ways to adapt skills, tactics and strategies and apply them with adherence to the rules of handball. Pupils will develop their resilience as they utilise the full rules and officiate their own games.

818.name: Net and wall games: understand effective performance in badminton
818.description: This unit will provide pupils with the opportunity to show commitment to developing their badminton skills further in both singles and doubles play. Pupils will also refine their skills at officiating, analysing performance and organising a fair competition.

819.name: Parkour: control, confidence and creativity
819.description: This unit will explore parkour with a focus on safety, fun and gradual skill development. Pupils will build their confidence and creativity tackling increasingly complex movements to include landing, rolling and precision jumps utilising a range of equipment and apparatus.
819.why: Pupils will already have used a variety of apparatus and covered the basic movements used for flight and safe landings. They will already be able to set up apparatus safely and recognise the importance of practising within their limits. Later in gymnastics they will apply these skills in trampolining with a focus on aesthetic appreciation and linking controlled movements.
prior: Pupils know how to move creatively showing variety including changes in levels, direction and using a range of body parts.
Pupils understand how to choreograph sequences that flow, incorporating a wide range of movements and balances.
Pupils are able to communicate and work well with others to overcome challenging tasks and solve problems.
Pupils show a willingness and desire to learn new and more complex skills.

820.name: Health and wellbeing: healthy leadership and effective reviewing skills
820.description: This unit will explore ways to lead, motivate and set SMART targets for themselves and others to help construct a meaningful fitness based activity. Pupils will also learn about some of the barriers to participation and how to review progress to help maintain motivation.
820.why: Pupils will already have developed their technique and understanding around body weight exercises and how to adjust a circuit training routine to maximise long term health and fitness benefits. They will combine this with ideas around effective leadership in a range of contexts. Later in health and wellbeing pupils will commit to a personalised fitness and learn more about nutrition, energy and the importance of hydration on physical and mental health.

817.name: Invasion games: adapt tactics and strategies through Gaelic football
817.description: This unit explores ways to adapt skills, tactics and strategies from football, rugby and handball to Gaelic football. Pupils will learn how to transfer skills of running with the ball, kicking and tackling plus new skills like fisting and soloing as they experience a game that will be new to most.
817.why: Pupils will already have developed their skills in contact and explored a wider range of tactics and strategies in a range of scenarios and specific sports like football, netball and rugby. This unit takes that understanding into the context of Gaelic football to enable pupils to experience a new game and transfer the relevant skills whilst learning a new set of rules. Later in invasion games they will apply tactics and strategies via games with different rules like handball, AFL and hockey.

823.name: Dance: the challenge
823.description: This unit utilises a pure approach that allows action-space-dynamics-relationships to be combined with fluency, accuracy and detail with each lesson being driven by a different stimuli to challenge creativity and problem solving drawing upon prior learning and preparing pupils for KS4.
823.why: This unit offers scope for pupils to draw upon prior learning and combine the performative, choreographic and stylistic features to produce a range of effects and be able to accurately identify the strengths and weaknesses in their own work and that of others. Pupils will be able to make recommendations for improvement. The abstract nature of the work encourages pupils to air original ideas building confidence and skills in performing, choreographing and appreciating dance and how it allies or responds to other artforms to deepen their understanding for further study and/or later life.

824.name: Net and wall games: overcome opponents in tennis challenges
824.description: This unit will provide pupils with the opportunity to transfer their hand-eye coordination and racket skills to tennis through a range of court games that develop skills further and introduce tennis specific rules, scoring and tactics. Pupils will be challenged to play by the rules.

825.name: Striking and fielding: officiating your own small sided cricket games
825.description: This unit will develop consistency, timing and fluency in the execution of batting, bowling and fielding skills as well as providing pupils with the opportunity to demonstrate integrity through officiating their own games.
825.why: Pupils will already have explored techniques for batting and overarm bowling in cricket whilst also improving their effectiveness fielding to deny runs. Later in striking and fielding games pupils will be challenged to adapt and transfer skills to softball whilst learning a new set of rules, techniques and tactics. 826.name: Athletics: fitness development of pace or power
826.description: This unit will develop pupils’ independence by supporting them to train and improve their pacing to sustain steady state running and/ or their power. Pupils will be exposed to different types of training as they apply the FITT principle to improve their fitness through track and field activities.

Later in athletics and health and wellbeing pupils will seek further opportunities to exercise in the outdoor environment.

827.name: Health and wellbeing: commitment to a personalised training plan
827.description: This unit will develop pupils’ ability to design and carry out a training programme with a focus on physical fitness and commitment to exercise that is enjoyable and tailored. Pupils will also learn about nutrition to help support them in living a healthy and active life beyond school.

Later in health and wellbeing pupils will explore a variety of additional approaches to holistic wellbeing to include couch to 5k; yoga, pilates and mindfulness; and exercises associated with martial arts and self-defence.

829.name: Invasion games: tactics and strategies in hockey
829.description: This unit explores a variety of tactics and strategies that can be transferred from other team games to hockey. Pupils’ persistence will be tested as they learn to apply the rules and find ways to tackle safely, strike the ball cleanly and avoid kicking the ball.
829.why: Pupils will already have developed ways to adapt skills, tactics and strategies from various forms of football but this unit places an implement in their hand which adds an extra dimension of challenge. 830.name: Gymnastics: technique, body control and constructive feedback in trampolining
830.description: This unit will develop skills in isolation and in combination with other techniques as part of a sequence of movements. To demonstrate control, aesthetics and fluency pupils will analyse and provide feedback to their peers. Pupils will also learn the basics about the axes of rotation.

846.name: Net and wall games: tactics and strategies in volleyball
846.description: This unit will build core skills and develop the use of game tactics to outwit opponents in pressurised situations. Pupils will sharpen their team working skills with a focus on managing conflict and generating the conditions for a great game regardless of the skill level of the participants.

831.name: Dance: phenomenal
831.description: This unit utilises a thematic approach to provide pupils with a platform to apply knowledge from other subject areas. 828.name: Invasion games: tactics and strategies in world games
828.description: This unit explores tactics and strategies that can be transferred to a variety of world games including Kabaddi, flag and Aussie Rules football (AFL). 834.name: Striking and fielding games: evaluate and improve performance in softball
834.description: This unit will develop batting, pitching and fielding skills unique to softball, such as using a glove and applying the rules around strikes and base running. Pupils will be challenged to evaluate both their own performance and that of others as they apply tenacity to this American game.
834.why: Pupils will already have explored rules, techniques and tactics for batting, bowling and fielding in rounders and cricket. Previous statistical and performance analysis skills will help with decision making. Pupils can take these skills, experiences and positive attitudes towards participation in a range of striking and fielding games into life with confidence and consequently lead healthy, active lives beyond school. 835.name: Outdoor adventurous activities: outdoor pursuits and team challenges
835.description: This unit will develop pupils’ independence and team working skills through outdoor pursuits and challenges. It will challenge pupils to think about and gain competence in lifestyle pursuits that encourage engagement beyond school whilst also developing physical fitness and connection to nature.
835.why: Pupils will already have found their struggle zone with regard to continuous running and explosive power tasks as well as facing physical and intellectual challenges. They will have learnt about fitness components, training methods and target setting but now get to channel this knowledge into more authentic environments and learn more about completing challenges in small groups. Pupils can take these skills, experiences and positive attitudes towards participation into life with confidence and consequently lead healthy, active lives beyond school.

836.name: Striking and fielding games: teaching others to play creative cricket games
836.description: This unit will develop pupils’ ability to teach each other and to play a variety of creative cricket games independently. Pupils will draw on their leadership skills to train, compete and perform.
836.why: Pupils will already have improved their consistency, timing and fluency in the execution of batting, bowling and fielding skills. They will design games that enable groups to become immersed in activity which will have a positive effect on mental health. Later in striking and fielding games pupils will be challenged to adapt and transfer skills to softball whilst learning a new set of rules, techniques and tactics. They will also be able to spectate and socialise in and around competitive sport with an appreciation and understanding of how to play.

1720.name: Kin-ball: communicating and solving problems through an inclusive game
1720.description: This unit explores a variety of tactics and strategies that can be transferred from other team games to kin-ball. Pupils will be challenged to demonstrate and develop their problem solving and communication skills in this unique and inclusive game with three teams.

This unit provides an opportunity to also learn about how positional play needs to be adapted to a unique game with three teams on the court at any one time. Later in invasion games they will apply more advanced tactics and strategies.

1736.name: Health and wellbeing: cardio tennis
1736.description: This unit will develop pupils’ understanding of a variety of ways to have fun whilst improving personal health and fitness. Their movement skills and cardiovascular endurance will improve whilst engaging in tennis based exercises.

1816.name: Remote learning: designing competitive games
1816.description: This unit offers opportunities to design games requiring ball control and tactical skill to achieve personal bests in complex tasks. Pupils will think creatively to adapt games to their environment and equipment, while challenging others to reach their own personal bests.
1816.why: Pupils will already have explored a variety of ways to control a ball using their hands, feet and other body parts. 1817.name: Remote learning: moving with athleticism
1817.description: This unit will support the development of complex and demanding movement combinations with a focus on purpose, precision and power. Pupils will accurately replicate complex movement combinations and reflect on their performance before refining and repeating.

1818.name: Remote learning: advanced dance
1818.description: This unit uses a thematic approach with body language and improvisation to express emotions and feelings. Pupils develop movement ideas beyond those introduced. Open-ended tasks encourage varied responses, building creative thinking and expressive skills.
1818.why: This unit offers scope for pupils to draw upon prior learning and combine performative, choreographic and stylistic features to produce a range of effects and be able to accurately identify the strengths and weaknesses in their own work. Pupils will be able to make recommendations for improvement.

1819.name: Remote learning: outdoor adventure activities and problem solving
1819.description: This unit explores pupils' ability to use a map, compass and plan a route. Developing the confidence to plan and follow movement routes accurately is a valuable cross curricular skill.
1819.why: Pupils will already have developed basic skills to operate within and as a team, but this unit challenges pupils to apply them in unique scenarios that require problem solving and creative thinking. Later in outdoor adventurous activities, pupils will get the opportunity to engage in activities beyond the school walls which will further develop their teamwork and leadership skills.
prior: Pupils know hope to solve problems by drawing on creative thinking and logic.

1820.name: Remote learning: health, fitness and wellbeing
1820.description: This unit will develop pupils’ ability to design and carry out a training programme with a focus on physical fitness and commitment to exercise that is enjoyable and tailored. Pupils will also learn about nutrition to help support them in living a healthy and active life beyond school.
1820.why: Pupils will have already enhanced their understanding of how to set SMART targets that support a meaningful and motivating fitness programme. They will have learnt about some of the benefits and types of training programmes available to them.

1569.name: Anatomy and physiology: the musculoskeletal system
1569.description: This unit will examine the structure and function of both the skeletal and the muscular systems. It includes locating major bones and muscles before defining and analysing what movements are possible at different joints.
1569.why: Key stage 3 PE and biology will have introduced pupils to some major bones and muscles. This unit cements this knowledge through the application of complex anatomical and physiological terminology. This forms the foundation of future sports science study and supports a deeper understanding of the impact of the musculoskeletal system on health, fitness and sporting performance. Later anatomy and physiology units will develop knowledge from this unit in the examination of other body systems, such as, the cardiovascular system and their application within movement analysis.
prior: Pupils know correct anatomical name and location of some bones (e.g. cranium, ribs, vertebrae, sternum and femur)
Pupils know correct anatomical name and location of some muscles (e.g. biceps, triceps, abdominals, quadriceps and hamstring)
Pupils know the name and location of major joints (hip, knee, elbow and shoulder)

1602.name: Anatomy and physiology: the cardio-respiratory system
1602.description: This unit will examine the structure and function of both the cardiovascular and respiratory systems. It includes the correct anatomical names and location of different chambers, valves and blood vessels as well as the pathway of air through to the alveoli and how gaseous exchange occurs.
1602.why: Pupils will already have a basic understanding of how the heart and lungs work to provide oxygen for life and energy for exercise. This unit cements that knowledge from key stage 3 PE and biology before further unpacking the application of complex anatomical and physiological terminology that forms the foundation of any future sports science study and also supports deeper understanding of health, fitness and sporting performance. Combined with previous knowledge about the musculo-skeletal system, pupils are put in a strong position to later understand aerobic and anaerobic exercise.
prior: Pupils can locate the heart and briefly describe its function
Pupils are able to locate the lungs and briefly describe their function
Pupils understand that oxygen from the atmosphere is inhaled for use by the body to provide energy (for life and exercise)

Pupils know that inhale refers to breathing in and exhale refers to breathing out
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1633.name: Anatomy and physiology: anaerobic and aerobic exercise
1633.description: This unit will explore the impact of varying the intensity and durations of exercise upon the build up of lactic acid and recovery rates. Exercises will be classified as either aerobic (with sufficient oxygen) or anaerobic (without sufficient oxygen).
1633.why: Pupils will already have experienced the impact of lactic acid build up on their ability to keep exercising. They will know how the muscles require oxygen to provide energy for movement and how the cardio-respiratory systems work together to transport that oxygen around the body as well as removing the waste product of carbon dioxide. They will later go on to unpick the specific short and long term effects of exercise on the body.
prior: Pupils understand that we must pace ourselves to run a long distance
Pupils understand that running at too faster pace results in muscle fatigue
Pupils have heard of the term lactic acid but don’t know much about it
Pupils know that oxygen is required for exercise and delivered to working muscles via the cardio-respiratory systems
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1636.name: Anatomy and physiology: the short and long term effects of exercise
1636.description: This unit will explore the immediate responses our bodies make to cope with the effects of exercise as well as the longer term adaptations it makes in response to training that enable us to cope better with exercise and improve performance.
1636.why: Pupils will already have in-depth understanding of the skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems as well as the impact of exercise intensity and duration on our ability to work aerobically. After they deepen their understanding of how the body responds to training they will move on to better understand how to train to improve health, fitness and sporting performance.
prior: Pupils know our heart rate and cardiac output increase when we exercise
Pupils know how our cardiac muscle enables increased blood supply to working muscles during exercise
Pupils know our breathing rate and minute ventilation increase when we exercise
Pupils understand training results in physiological changes that make exercise become easier
Pupils know that our heart rate gradually returns to resting levels of about 72 BPM after exercise
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1629.name: Movement analysis and basic biomechanics
1629.description: This unit will explore basic principles of movement and their effect on sporting performance to include the classification of levers, planes of movement and axis of rotation. This understanding enables pupils to maximise efficiency of movement or generate more power.
1629.why: Pupils will already have in-depth understanding of how muscles work in antagonistic pairs across a joint to create movement via the leverage of bones. After they appreciate the three classes of lever and different planes/ axes our bodies can move in they will be in a strong position to develop their understanding of how different types of training impact positively on sporting performance. This unit links nicely with learning from maths and physics to form the foundations of biomechanical understanding.
prior: Pupils know the name and location of different joints in the human body (e.g. knee, ankle and elbow)
Pupils know that muscles work in antagonistic pairs across a joint to create movement via leverage of bones
Pupils know that muscles create movement by contracting and pulling one bone to articulate against another bone via connected tendons
Pupils understand that some movements and sports require greater force of contraction whereas others require prolonged moderate intensity contractions

1639.name: Physical training: health and fitness
1639.description: This unit will explore the relationship between health, fitness, exercise and performance before unpacking the different components of fitness. This understanding will include key definitions, how to test and train each but also which components are most important for different sports.
1639.why: Pupils will already have a basic appreciation of how fitness comprises different elements that are important to a greater or lesser extent depending on the activity. From the applied anatomy and physiology units they will also have an in-depth understanding of how our bodies respond to exercise and adapt to cope better after a period of training. Later in physical training they will explore principles and methods of training as well as how to reduce the risk of injury through overtraining or poor programming.
prior: Pupils know the names of and examples of a few components of fitness in action (e.g. endurance, strength, speed, flexibility, power, agility, balance and coordination)
Pupils know that exercise and regular training are required to improve fitness and sporting performance
Pupils understand that health has physical and mental components but perhaps not appreciate the social element

1643.name: Physical training: principles of training
1643.description: This unit will explore the guidelines or principles that we should follow when training to improve health, fitness and sporting performance.
1643.why: Pupils will continue to develop their understanding of how to train for improved everyday health and/ or sporting performance. From the applied anatomy and physiology units they will have an in-depth understanding of how our bodies respond to exercise and adapt to cope better after a period of training and this knowledge lays the foundations for understanding these training principles. Later in physical training they will discover different methods of training that are of benefit to different individuals at different times in their training programmes.
prior: Pupils know that it is important to train regularly but also to have rest days for recovery

1646.name: Physical training: methods of training
1646.description: This unit will describe and enable pupils to experience different types of training before analysing which ones are most suited to different types of sporting performers.
1646.why: Pupils will continue to develop their understanding of different ways to train for improved everyday health and/ or sporting performance. From the earlier physical training units pupils will understand the components of fitness that should be prioritised for different sports and/ or playing positions to inform which types of training are most relevant and beneficial. Later in physical training they will consider injuries and injury prevention as well as performance enhancing drugs.

Pupils know the difference between continuous (non-stop) and interval (reps and sets) training
Pupils know the importance of a warm up to reduce the risk of pulling a muscle

1649.name: Physical training: injury and injury prevention
1649.description: This unit unpicks the many factors to be considered to prevent injury in sport. It focussess on the effective delivery of both warm up and cool down components of training.
1649.why: Pupils will build on basic understanding of injury and injury prevention gained through key stage 3 and their involvement in sport and physical activity. From the earlier physical training units they will understand which components of fitness are most important for different sports. They will appreciate the principles and methods of training that are most beneficial for different individuals. Later in physical training they will consider performance enhancing drugs and why some athletes are tempted to use them as well as gaining an appreciation of the negative side effects of specific drugs.

1626.name: Use of data
1626.description: This unit supports pupils to be able to demonstrate an understanding of how both qualitative and quantitative data are collected, presented and analysed to include tables and graphs.
1626.why: Pupils will further develop their understanding of how data relating to physical activity participation or sports performance can be collected, compared to normative data and presented to help inform analysis. As a synoptic skill that is required to tackle aspects of both paper 1 and paper 2 content this unit will draw on examples from a number of topic areas and be further explored in socio-cultural and health, fitness and well-being units.

1619.name: Non-examined assessment: preparing for the written coursework
1619.description: This unit will provide guidance and support to enable pupils to successfully complete their exam board specific coursework.
1619.why: Pupils will already know how the body systems, physical fitness and sport specific training contribute to optimum performance. This unit provides the necessary guidance to complete their written coursework worth 10% of their final mark. Later in the programme they will need to apply this knowledge independently to produce their written work with limited teacher input and in line with awarding organisation (exam board) guidelines.

Pupils understand the different components of fitness and how they contribute to well-being and/ or sporting performance
Pupils can select strengths and weaknesses in a sport of their choice
threads: Think: knowledge of rules, tactics, strategies and compositional ideas

1606.name: Non-examined assessment: athletics practical
1606.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios across all athletic disciplines. As a popular individual sport offered by many pupils it will cover sprinting, middle distance, jumping, shot put and javelin events.
1606.why: Pupils will already know the correct technique and relevant rules to different athletics disciplines from key stage 3 PE. This unit provides the opportunity to evaluate technique and record times/ distances to highlight pupils who would perform well at athletics as one of their chosen practical sports. Positioned during the summer term of year 10 it will encourage engagement in extracurricular opportunities to include local competitions to improve performance further.
prior: Pupils know the importance of a sprint start and staying low in the drive phase of sprint events
Pupils understand the importance of not falling back in long and triple jump as measurement is from the furthest back point and you must take off without crossing the board
Pupils understand the importance of angle of release and not crossing the line when throwing
Pupils understand the importance of pacing in middle distance events
Pupils are able to make connections with sprinting events as anaerobic and middle distance runs as aerobic and trying to stay just below the lactate threshold
threads: Think: knowledge of rules, tactics, strategies and compositional ideas

1610.name: Non-examined assessment: football practical
1610.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios in association football. As a popular team sport offered by many pupils it will cover passing/ receiving, dribbling, shooting, ball control, tackling and decision making.
1610.why: Pupils will already know the correct technique and relevant rules for football from key stage 3 PE. This unit builds upon this by providing the opportunity to evaluate technique and practise some observation and analysis skills. Positioned during the autumn term of year 10, it will encourage engagement in extracurricular opportunities, including local clubs and competitions, which will allow further improvement of performance. This unit will help to prepare students for the practical GCSE moderation in Year 11.

Pupils understand how to defend, mark and jockey players

Pupils understand the difference between qualitative and quantitative data through observation and analysis of performance

1722.name: Non-examined assessment: basketball practical

1570.name: Anatomy and physiology: the musculoskeletal system
1570.description: This unit will examine the structure and function of both the skeletal and the muscular systems. It includes locating major bones and muscles before defining and analysing what movements are possible at different joints.
1570.why: Key stage 3 PE and biology will have introduced pupils to some major bones and muscles. This unit cements this knowledge through the application of complex anatomical and physiological terminology. This forms the foundation of future sports science study and supports a deeper understanding of the impact of the musculoskeletal system on health, fitness and sporting performance. Later anatomy and physiology units will develop knowledge from this unit in the examination of other body systems, such as, the cardiovascular system and their application within movement analysis.
prior: Pupils know correct anatomical name and location of some bones (e.g. cranium, ribs, vertebrae, sternum and femur)
Pupils know correct anatomical name and location of some muscles (e.g. biceps, triceps, abdominals, quadriceps and hamstring)
Pupils know the name and location of major joints (hip, knee, elbow and shoulder)
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1603.name: Anatomy and physiology: the cardio-respiratory system
1603.description: This unit will examine the structure and function of both the cardiovascular and respiratory systems. It includes the correct anatomical names and location of different chambers, valves and blood vessels as well as the pathway of air through to the alveoli and how gaseous exchange occurs.
1603.why: Pupils will already have a basic understanding of how the heart and lungs work to provide oxygen for life and energy for exercise. This unit cements that knowledge from key stage 3 PE and biology before further unpacking the application of complex anatomical and physiological terminology that forms the foundation of any future sports science study and also supports deeper understanding of health, fitness and sporting performance. Combined with previous knowledge about the musculo-skeletal system, pupils are put in a strong position to later understand aerobic and anaerobic exercise.
prior: Pupils can locate the heart and briefly describe its function
Pupils are able to locate the lungs and briefly describe their function
Pupils understand that oxygen from the atmosphere is inhaled for use by the body to provide energy (for life and exercise)
Pupils know how heart rate responds to exercise
Pupils know how breathing rate responds to exercise
Pupils know that inhale refers to breathing in and exhale refers to breathing out
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1634.name: Anatomy and physiology: anaerobic and aerobic exercise
1634.description: This unit will explore the impact of varying the intensity and durations of exercise upon the build up of lactic acid and recovery rates. Exercises will be classified as either aerobic (with sufficient oxygen) or anaerobic (without sufficient oxygen).
1634.why: Pupils will already have experienced the impact of lactic acid build up on their ability to keep exercising. They will know how the muscles require oxygen to provide energy for movement and how the cardio-respiratory systems work together to transport that oxygen around the body as well as removing the waste product of carbon dioxide. They will later go on to unpick the specific short and long term effects of exercise on the body.
prior: Pupils understand that we must pace ourselves to run a long distance
Pupils understand that running at too faster pace results in muscle fatigue
Pupils have heard of the term lactic acid but don’t know much about it
Pupils know that oxygen is required for exercise and delivered to working muscles via the cardio-respiratory systems
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1637.name: Anatomy and physiology: the short and long term effects of exercise
1637.description: This unit will explore the immediate responses our bodies make to cope with the effects of exercise as well as the longer term adaptations it makes in response to training that enable us to cope better with exercise and improve performance.
1637.why: Pupils will already have in-depth understanding of the skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems as well as the impact of exercise intensity and duration on our ability to work aerobically. After they deepen their understanding of how the body responds to training they will move on to better understand how to train to improve health, fitness and sporting performance.
prior: Pupils know our heart rate and cardiac output increase when we exercise
Pupils know how our cardiac muscle enables increased blood supply to working muscles during exercise
Pupils know our breathing rate and minute ventilation increase when we exercise
Pupils understand training results in physiological changes that make exercise become easier
Pupils know that our heart rate gradually returns to resting levels of about 72 BPM after exercise
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1630.name: Movement analysis and basic biomechanics
1630.description: This unit will explore basic principles of movement and their effect on sporting performance to include the classification of levers, planes of movement and axis of rotation. This understanding enables pupils to maximise efficiency of movement or generate more power.
1630.why: Pupils will already have in-depth understanding of how muscles work in antagonistic pairs across a joint to create movement via the leverage of bones. After they appreciate the three classes of lever and different planes/ axes our bodies can move in they will be in a strong position to develop their understanding of how different types of training impact positively on sporting performance. This unit links nicely with learning from maths and physics to form the foundations of biomechanical understanding.
prior: Pupils know the name and location of different joints in the human body (e.g. knee, ankle and elbow)
Pupils know that muscles work in antagonistic pairs across a joint to create movement via leverage of bones
Pupils know that muscles create movement by contracting and pulling one bone to articulate against another bone via connected tendons
Pupils understand that some movements and sports require greater force of contraction whereas others require prolonged moderate intensity contractions
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1640.name: Physical training: health and fitness
1640.description: This unit will explore the relationship between health, fitness, exercise and performance before unpacking the different components of fitness. This understanding will include key definitions, how to test and train each but also which components are most important for different sports.
1640.why: Pupils will already have a basic appreciation of how fitness comprises different elements that are important to a greater or lesser extent depending on the activity. From the applied anatomy and physiology units they will also have an in-depth understanding of how our bodies respond to exercise and adapt to cope better after a period of training. Later in physical training they will explore principles and methods of training as well as how to reduce the risk of injury through overtraining or poor programming.
prior: Pupils know the names of and examples of a few components of fitness in action (e.g. endurance, strength, speed, flexibility, power, agility, balance and coordination)
Pupils know that exercise and regular training are required to improve fitness and sporting performance
Pupils understand that health has physical and mental components but perhaps not appreciate the social element
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1644.name: Physical training: principles of training
1644.description: This unit will explore the guidelines or principles that we should follow when training to improve health, fitness and sporting performance.
1644.why: Pupils will continue to develop their understanding of how to train for improved everyday health and/ or sporting performance. From the applied anatomy and physiology units they will have an in-depth understanding of how our bodies respond to exercise and adapt to cope better after a period of training and this knowledge lays the foundations for understanding these training principles. Later in physical training they will discover different methods of training that are of benefit to different individuals at different times in their training programmes.
prior: Pupils know that it is important to train regularly but also to have rest days for recovery
Pupils know what a typical resting heart rate is and how to calculate your maximum heart rate (220 minus your age)
Pupils understand the heart rate response to exercise
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1647.name: Physical training: methods of training
1647.description: This unit will describe and enable pupils to experience different types of training before analysing which ones are most suited to different types of sporting performers.
1647.why: Pupils will continue to develop their understanding of different ways to train for improved everyday health and/ or sporting performance. From the earlier physical training units pupils will understand the components of fitness that should be prioritised for different sports and/ or playing positions to inform which types of training are most relevant and beneficial. Later in physical training they will consider injuries and injury prevention as well as performance enhancing drugs.
prior: Pupils know what basic circuit training includes
Pupils know the difference between continuous (non-stop) and interval (reps and sets) training
Pupils know the importance of a warm up to reduce the risk of pulling a muscle
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1650.name: Physical training: injury, injury prevention and performance enhancing drugs
1650.description: This unit unpicks the many factors to be considered to prevent injury in sport. It focussess on the effective delivery of both warm up and cool down components of training.
1650.why: Pupils will build on basic understanding of injury and injury prevention gained through key stage 3 and their involvement in sport and physical activity. From the earlier physical training units they will understand which components of fitness are most important for different sports. They will appreciate the principles and methods of training that are most beneficial for different individuals. Later in physical training they will consider performance enhancing drugs and why some athletes are tempted to use them as well as gaining an appreciation of the negative side effects of specific drugs.
prior: Pupils understand the parts to a warm up and their impact on reducing the risk of injury
Pupils have heard about different types of injuries in a range of sports

1627.name: Use of data
1627.description: This unit supports pupils to be able to demonstrate an understanding of how both qualitative and quantitative data are collected, presented and analysed to include tables and graphs.

1648.description: This unit will describe and enable pupils to experience different types of training before analysing which ones are most suited to different types of sporting performers.
1648.why: Pupils will continue to develop their understanding of different ways to train for improved everyday health and/ or sporting performance. From the earlier physical training units pupils will understand the components of fitness that should be prioritised for different sports and/ or playing positions to inform which types of training are most relevant and beneficial. Later in physical training they will consider injuries and injury prevention as well as performance enhancing drugs.
prior: Pupils know what basic circuit training includes
Pupils know the difference between continuous (non-stop) and interval (reps and sets) training
Pupils know the importance of a warm up to reduce the risk of pulling a muscle
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1651.name: Physical training: injury and injury prevention
1651.description: This unit unpicks the many factors to be considered to prevent injury in sport. It focussess on the effective delivery of both warm up and cool down components of training.
1651.why: Pupils will build on basic understanding of injury and injury prevention gained through key stage 3 and their involvement in sport and physical activity. From the earlier physical training units they will understand which components of fitness are most important for different sports. They will appreciate the principles and methods of training that are most beneficial for different individuals. Later in physical training they will consider performance enhancing drugs and why some athletes are tempted to use them as well as gaining an appreciation of the negative side effects of specific drugs.
prior: Pupils understand the parts to a warm up and their impact on reducing the risk of injury
Pupils have heard about different types of injuries in a range of sports
threads: Think: knowledge of healthy, active living

1628.name: Use of data
1628.description: This unit supports pupils to be able to demonstrate an understanding of how both qualitative and quantitative data are collected, presented and analysed to include tables and graphs.
1628.why: Pupils will further develop their understanding of how data relating to physical activity participation or sports performance can be collected, compared to normative data and presented to help inform analysis. As a synoptic skill that is required to tackle aspects of both paper 1 and paper 2 content this unit will draw on examples from a number of topic areas and be further explored in socio-cultural and health, fitness and well-being units.
prior: Pupils know what a graph is and which the x and y axis are
Pupils understand how data can be presented in different forms of line, bar and pie charts

1622.name: Non-examined assessment: preparing for the written coursework
1622.description: This unit will provide guidance and support to enable pupils to successfully complete their exam board specific coursework.
1622.why: Pupils will already know how the body systems, physical fitness and sport specific training contribute to optimum performance. This unit provides the necessary guidance to complete their written coursework worth 10% of their final mark. Later in the programme they will need to apply this knowledge independently to produce their written work with limited teacher input and in line with awarding organisation (exam board) guidelines.
prior: Pupils understand that regular exercise is required to build fitness
Pupils understand the different components of fitness and how they contribute to well-being and/ or sporting performance
Pupils can select strengths and weaknesses in a sport of their choice

1608.name: Non-examined assessment: athletics practical
1608.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios across all athletic disciplines. As a popular individual sport offered by many pupils it will cover sprinting, middle distance, jumping, shot put and javelin events.
1608.why: Pupils will already know the correct technique and relevant rules to different athletics disciplines from key stage 3 PE. This unit provides the opportunity to evaluate technique and record times/ distances to highlight pupils who would perform well at athletics as one of their chosen practical sports. Positioned during the summer term of year 10 it will encourage engagement in extracurricular opportunities to include local competitions to improve performance further.
prior: Pupils know the importance of a sprint start and staying low in the drive phase of sprint events

Pupils understand the importance of pacing in middle distance events
Pupils are able to make connections with sprinting events as anaerobic and middle distance runs as aerobic and trying to stay just below the lactate threshold

1612.name: Non-examined assessment: football practical
1612.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios in association football. As a popular team sport offered by many pupils it will cover passing/ receiving, dribbling, shooting, ball control, tackling and decision making.
1612.why: Pupils will already know the correct technique and relevant rules for football from key stage 3 PE. This unit builds upon this by providing the opportunity to evaluate technique and practise some observation and analysis skills. Positioned during the autumn term of year 10, it will encourage engagement in extracurricular opportunities, including local clubs and competitions, which will allow further improvement of performance. This unit will help to prepare students for the practical GCSE moderation in Year 11.

1615.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios in netball. 1618.name: Non-examined assessment: rugby league practical
1618.description: This unit provides pupils with the knowledge and opportunity to replicate skills in isolation and in performance scenarios in rugby. As a popular team sport offered by many pupils it will cover passing/ receiving, ball handling, tackling, rucking, scrums, line outs, kicking and decision making.
1618.why: Pupils will already know the basics of play and relevant rules for rugby from key stage 3 PE. 837.name: Health and wellbeing: HIIT and couch to 5k team challenges to develop fitness
837.description: This unit will develop pupils’ understanding of the principles of training through a running programme that stretches them as an individual but also their contribution to a team. Their cardiovascular endurance will improve whilst taking responsibility for their own training.
837.why: Pupils will already have designed their own training programme to work on aspects of physical fitness that matter to them. This unit challenges them to work together towards common goals of improved cardiovascular endurance and the power of taking responsibility for following a prescribed programme based on current fitness levels. Later in health and wellbeing pupils will explore approaches to holistic wellbeing to include yoga, pilates and mindfulness; and exercises associated with martial arts and self-defence.

Pupils understand that regular training and progression will result in improvements in fitness.
Pupils are able to appreciate the physical and psychological effect of exercise.

838.name: Invasion games: problem solving with tactics and strategies through T1 rugby
838.description: This unit challenges pupils to problem solve and make good decisions under pressure in T1 rugby games and scenarios. Pupils will apply more advanced tactics and strategies whilst securing their understanding of the nuances in the laws of the game.
838.why: Pupils will already have developed a variety of skills, tactics and strategies from various games with the ball in hand, at feet and in rugby and other invasion game situations (such as Kabaddi), but this unit requires pupils to learn how to problem solve in a different version of the game. Later in invasion games they will apply more advanced tactics and strategies to other new games.
