3289.correction: Improvements in speed and fitness for middle distance running can also come from running easy efforts. This builds aerobic fitness and gives the individual a strong base where over time the same effort will be maintained but at a faster pace.

1806.belief: A common mistake in the triple jump is the athlete collapses the middle 'step phase' rather than getting equal height and distance from every phase.
1806.statement: A common mistake in the triple jump is the athlete collapses the middle 'step phase' rather than getting equal height and distance from every phase.
1806.correction: Emphasis on all phases of the jump should be practised, especially the step phase, with height and efficiency. All phases of the triple jump should contribute to an equal proportion of distance e.g. 2m x2m x2m

3291.belief: If you get off the mat before the bar falls it will still count as a successful jump.
3291.statement: If you get off the mat before the bar falls it will still count as a successful jump.
3291.correction: If the bar falls then the jump does not count, even if the jumper has left the mat. Every attempt should be made to clear the bar rather than rushing the landing and clearing the mat quickly.

10313.belief: You throw a shot in the shot put.
10313.statement: You throw a shot in the shot put.
10313.correction: The shot put does not require any rotation around a joint. It is pushed from under the chin and touching the neck. A throw action will likely lead to injury due to the weight of the shot. However, "throw" is standard terminology for this event.

9640.belief: Strength and power are more important than technique when throwing a javelin far.
9640.statement: Strength and power are more important than technique when throwing a javelin far.
9640.correction: While strength and power are both important, too much strength and not enough time focusing on technique, can impact the accuracy of the throw. A well executed throw will travel further than just force alone.

10315.belief: All throwing events have the same technique.
10315.statement: All throwing events have the same technique.
10315.correction: While there is a common core technique across all throwing events, each event has a unique set of technical elements that range from the grip, stance, release and recovery phases.

602.belief: A belief that our identity is fixed and permanent.
602.statement: A belief that our identity is fixed and permanent.
602.correction: Who we are and how that is expressed can be changed, and is likely to shift throughout our life. We can communicate who we are through our expression, how we dress, how we speak and by taking part in activities that are important to us.

6113.belief: Only performers participate in competitive events.
6113.statement: Pupils believe only performers participate in competitive events.
6113.correction: Competitions depend on various roles to run safely and efficiently. Performers can only participate if officials and organisers set up the event correctly.

5696.belief: Poor sporting behaviour is only related to people who spectate or support the events.
5696.statement: Poor sporting behaviour is only related to people who spectate or support the events.
5696.correction: Everyone involved in the competition is responsible for how they behave and showing good sporting behaviour. This includes supporters, performers and officials. Everyone's role is to ensure the event remains safe, fair and enjoyable for all.

8616.statement: Pupils wait until they have the baton before starting to run in a relay.
8616.correction: Outgoing runners need to move to the start of the exchange zone and start their run sooner to accelerate as they are handed the baton on the move. Practise the technique from stationary to running to ensure action is well rehearsed.

10113.belief: Tackling harder always makes it more effective.
10113.statement: Tackling harder always makes it more effective.
10113.correction: Controlled technique, not force, makes a tackle successful and reduces the chance of injury or penalties.

6704.statement: Pupils forget that after making a tackle, they need to get back onside in a straight line.
6704.correction: Response: after a tackle, the whole defensive line need to be back onside 10m from the play of the ball. If you are not moving as a flat line, you leave gaps for attackers to break through.

8146.belief: When you are player-to -player marking it is only about being an individual.
8146.statement: Pupils think that when you are player-to -player marking it is only about being an individual.
8146.correction: Defenders must communicate, adjust to overloads and support each other. If one defender gets beaten, others need to be ready to help. Marking your player is just one part of working together to stop the attack.

8305.belief: Tackling a raider individually is the only option.
8305.statement: Pupils think that tackling a raider individually is the only option.
8305.correction: In Kabaddi, Raiders have 30 seconds to make the raid and get back across the half way line. As a result, if the defense hold up the raider until their time runs out, it is an unsuccessful raid and the raider doesn't score.

8006.belief: If they miss a tackle, they should just give up.
8006.statement: Pupils think if they miss a tackle, they should just give up.
8006.correction: Pupils need to show determination to chase back and continue to pressure the attack, even if they miss a tackle.

7732.belief: You can constantly change directions when chasing.
7732.statement: Pupils think you can constantly change directions when chasing.
7732.correction: Remind pupils that in Kho Kho, chasers cannot change direction freely. They must run around a turning pole to change direction. Turning mid-court is a foul.

8308.belief: To take 3 steps with the ball, you have to be dribbling.
8308.statement: Pupils think that to take 3 steps with the ball, you have to be dribbling.
8308.correction: You only need to dribble if you want to take more than 3 steps. Once you catch the ball, you're allowed 3 steps without dribbling.

8022.belief: The only movement that is important is the movement with the ball.
8022.statement: Pupils think the only movement that is important is the movement with the ball.
8022.correction: Movement off the ball is just as important, it helps create space and supports the player in possession.

8244.belief: The shooter is allowed in the D to score (like netball).
8244.statement: Pupils think the shooter is allowed in the D to score (like netball).
8244.correction: The only person allowed in the D is the goalkeeper, shooters have to shoot from outside the D, otherwise the goal doesn't count.

8021.belief: You should only move slowly with the ball so you don't lose posession.
8021.statement: Pupils think you should only move slowly with the ball so you don't lose posession.
8021.correction: Moving fast with the ball can create more opportunities to beat defenders, create space and keep the attacking momentum strong.

8369.belief: The only way to defend is to mark 1 player on the opposite team.
8369.statement: Pupils think the only way to defend is to mark 1 player on the opposite team.
8369.correction: Sometimes moving as a unit, where you shift together, can prevent any of the attackers from making a break and getting the ball up the court.

5590.belief: Only the player taking the throw-off needs to be in their own half.
5590.statement: Only the player taking the throw-off needs to be in their own half.
5590.correction: All players must be in their own half before the throw-off is taken, not just the thrower.

6177.statement: Pupils call their score first and get confused which side they should serve from.
6177.correction: You should always call the serving player's/team's score first. If their score is even, then they serve from the right, whereas if their score is odd, they serve from the left.

7557.statement: Pupils swing when hitting drop shots and net shots.
7557.correction: By reducing your backswing and almost eliminating your follow through, you will be able to perform more successful drop shots and net shots that trickle just over the net and put your opponent under more pressure.

6774.statement: Pupils hit all shots with a similar technique and avoid high risk, powerful smashes to avoid losing points.
6774.correction: Practising smash shots is necessary in order to take your game to the next level.

8618.statement: Pupils wait until their opponent hits the shuttle before starting to initiate movement to retrieve it.
8618.correction: If you wait until you know where the shuttle is going before starting to move, you will often be too late to get to it. Instead, pre-load your legs with a split step to trigger an explosive lunge to reach the shuttle faster.

6375.statement: Pupils don't adapt their court position based on where their partner is and where the shuttle has been hit.
6375.correction: Work together to cover the court. If your partner is at the front of the court then it is important to step back to cover the back of the court. However, it is typically easier to assume side-by-side positioning and cover half the court each.

6835.statement: Pupils instinctively want to work with their best friend and/or the 'best' partner.
6835.correction: When playing matches, it's fulfilling when a competition is balanced and offers an equal chance of winning. To achieve this, pair up pupils based on current performance levels or agree a number of starting points to give to one of the people/teams.

7567.statement: Pupils often take-off with the wrong foot when performing the thief vault or they take-off too close to the obstacle.
7567.correction: Work on take-off in isolation, focusing on taking-off with the outside foot and ensuring there is enough space between them and the obstacle to ensure continued flow through the vault.

8482.statement: Pupils will often underestimate or overestimate the distance, leading to overshooting the jump or falling too short.
8482.correction: Emphasise that hitting the edge of the mat is crucial, therefore they should gradually increase the distance to find the correct one for them. This will also need to be adjusted when they add a run up.

6899.statement: Pupils often look down at their feet and lack core stability when balancing, which shifts their centre of gravity so they are off balance.
6899.correction: Pupils should focus on looking slightly forward on a stable point at eye level and learn how to engage their core when balancing.

2941.belief: Fear of falling or not clearing the obstacle can lead to hesitation which can then affect the flow and overall success of the vault.
2941.statement: Fear of falling or not clearing the obstacle can lead to hesitation which can then affect the flow and overall success of the vault.
2941.correction: Gradual progression and practising on lower obstacles can help build confidence.

5694.belief: Poor foot placement on the wall when performing tic tacs and wall runs can result in poor technique and a weak push off. Poor control on landing is also a common issue with Tic Tacs and Wall Runs.
5694.statement: Poor foot placement on the wall when performing tic tacs and wall runs can result in poor technique and a weak push off. Poor control on landing is also a common issue with Tic Tacs and Wall Runs.
5694.correction: Use visual cues (e.g. chalk marks or splat spots/cones) on the wall to show the ideal contact point. Also use markers to indicate where to land and teach pupils to land quietly and stick their landing.

6189.statement: Pupils may choose obstacles that don't link well and therefore don't allow for smooth transitions.
6189.correction: Provide lots of route planning support and examples/advice throughout the lesson.

7793.belief: All effective leaders are loud and shout to be heard.
7793.statement: Pupils think all effective leaders are loud and shout to be heard.
7793.correction: It is common to hear a leader with a voice which is projected when communicating. However, there is so much to effective leadership beyond verbal communication, such as, active listening, knowing your team and showing empathy, to name a few.

7873.belief: A goal or a target it the end product or outcome to be achieved.
7873.statement: Pupils think a goal or a target it the end product or outcome to be achieved.
7873.correction: A goal can be based on outcome, however it can also be a goal set about the performance or process of doing something. For example, building a 3-2-1 pyramid in the quickest time compared to building the 3-2-1 pyramid without dropping any objects.

7959.belief: Leading is just about giving instructions.
7959.statement: Pupils think leading is just about giving instructions.
7959.correction: A ledaer also requires active listening and the time and confidence to provide feedback on what has been completed well and how things can be improved.

8258.belief: To solve a problem has a just one single option.
8258.statement: Pupils think to solve a problem has a just one single option.
8258.correction: Problem solving is not linear, nor is there only one universal problem solving technique. The right approach depends on the nature of the problem in a specific context.

7730.belief: Conflict is negative and should always be avoided.
7730.statement: Pupils think conflict is negative and should always be avoided.
7730.correction: In reality, resolving conflict is an important lifeskill that can also be the catalyst for creativity and innovation. It can challenge assumptions but does need to be managed constructively.

7729.correction: Fluctuations in confidence are very normal. It is not a static state and often determined by the environment your are in and any previous experience you have of that environment.

7875.belief: Good leaders are born like that.
7875.statement: Pupils think good leaders are born like that.
7875.correction: Effective leadership is developed through experience and learning from mistakes.

8180.belief: Punctuality is merely about turning up to lessons on time.
8180.statement: Pupils think punctuality is merely about turning up to lessons on time.
8180.correction: Punctuality is linked to arrival time, but is also about completing tasks on time and being respectful for the time of others. This is achieved by being organised, fulfilling the task and being dependable.

7805.belief: Emotional intelligence is simply about being nice or positive and is a fixed trait.
7805.statement: Pupils think emotional intelligence is simply about being nice or positive and is a fixed trait.
7805.correction: Emotional intelligence is recognising, expressing and managing emotions. It can be developed and improved with practice and feedback.

7600.belief: Being adaptable as a leader is when there is a forced change.
7600.statement: Pupils think being adaptable as a leader is when there is a forced change.
7600.correction: Adaptability for an effective leader is when it is always happening and the leader is responding to how the needs of the group are being met and if the environment is working or not.

7892.belief: HIIT is only for experienced athletes.
7892.statement: Pupils think HIIT is only for experienced athletes.
7892.correction: HIIT can be modified to suit all fitness levels. It can be a valuable and quick tool to improve many components of fitness. The intervals can be shorter for beginners and the exercises less intense.

8236.belief: Self-assessment is similar to being assessed in something.
8236.statement: Pupils think self-assessment is similar to being assessed in something.
8236.correction: Self-assessment is an opportunity to reflect and does not count towards any assessment. It is positive. Leaders are able to grow from self-assessments as they recognise strengths, but more importantly, identify keys areas of improvement.

9412.belief: When soloing the ball, pupils don't flick their toe upwards causing the ball to travel in front of them. When passing, pupils throw the ball, forgetting the correct open or closed hand passing action.
9412.statement: When soloing the ball, pupils don't flick their toe upwards causing the ball to travel in front of them. When passing, pupils throw the ball, forgetting the correct open or closed hand passing action.
9412.correction: When the foot impacts the ball, flick your toes up so the ball travels back into the hands. Pupils should spend a lot of time repeating their hand passing skills to avoid throwing the ball when under pressure.

3949.belief: Kicks may lack the necessary power or accuracy, or they might often miss their target. High catches can be intimidating and pupils may mistime their jump.
3949.statement: Kicks may lack the necessary power or accuracy, or they might often miss their target. High catches can be intimidating and pupils may mistime their jump.
3949.correction: Focus on good technique before increasing distance or adding movements to kicks. When performing a high catch, track the ball early and use the jumping technique to meet the ball when it is at its highest point.

8608.statement: Pupils use the wrong hand which leads to fouls and ineffective tackles, or they dive into the tackle, allowing attackers to easily sidestep away.
8608.correction: Always use the nearest hand to flick the ball away. Stay balanced when tackling, moving your feet quickly and timing the tackle properly.

2919.belief: The fake is too subtle and not performed at a fast enough pace. Pupils make fake too early so it is easy to read.
2919.statement: The fake is too subtle and not performed at a fast enough pace. Pupils make fake too early so it is easy to read.
2919.correction: Use clear and exaggerated movements when faking and shift your weight explosively. Wait until the defender is close before performing your faked movement.

7454.statement: Pupils may struggle to recognise the right movement to execute different strategies, which results in losing possession or missed opportunities.
7454.correction: Break down the games so you can focus on good decision making. Stop game play when a poor is decision made to ask pupils to identify and resolve the problem.

5597.belief: When playing as part of a bigger team, pupils often bunch around the ball and do not hold their shape. They can also be more static off the ball thinking that teammates will be available for a pass.
5597.statement: When playing as part of a bigger team, pupils often bunch around the ball and do not hold their shape. They can also be more static off the ball thinking that teammates will be available for a pass.
5597.correction: Reduce the numbers on each team, assign clear roles or freeze the play regularly to demonstrate where players should be. Focus on movement off the ball as soon as players have passed.

5459.belief: When performing in a group formation, this should always be in unison.
5459.statement: When performing in a group formation, this should always be in unison.
5459.correction: Unison can be highly effective in clear formations as this also communicates unity and power, but other choreographic relationships such as canon, mirroring or contact work also add interest and are visually exciting to watch.

2169.belief: Dancers have to be silent when performing.
2169.statement: Dancers have to be silent when performing.
2169.correction: Whilst this is usually the case, dance often connects with other artforms and occasionally dancers may also speak, sing or make sounds through body percussion (e.g. clapping or stamping).

4725.belief: Motif variation and motif development are the same thing.
4725.statement: Motif variation and motif development are the same thing.
4725.correction: Variation and development are both methods of motif manipulation. However, during variation, the action content remains the same but how it is presented can be changed. Whereas, development involves significant alteration to the actions themselves.

64.belief: It is acceptable to copy the work of others in dance.
64.statement: It is acceptable to copy the work of others in dance.
64.correction: Copying the work of others and passing it off as your own is known as plagiarism. However, identifying features that are common to a dance style and applying it to your choreography is different, but should remain respectful to the original source.

500.belief: The audience are always directly facing the stage/performers.
500.statement: The audience are always directly facing the stage/performers.
500.correction: Whilst most theatres use an 'end on' arrangement, this isn't always the case. Fashion shows traditionally use a 'thrust' stage, lecture-demonstrations might use 'in the round' and performances such as Mummers' plays, may use 'promenade'.

5454.belief: Performers should always look straight ahead and project to their audience.
5454.statement: Performers should always look straight ahead and project to their audience.
5454.correction: In many styles, the connection to the audience is an important part of the performance. This can also be achieved by including a change of focus to communicate the performer's mood or intention, or to indicate what the audience should be looking at.

7203.statement: Pupils rush to play full court from the baseline before they have the racket skills to direct the ball accurately and keep a rally going.
7203.correction: Tennis can be a frustrating game with a lot of fetching mis-hit balls. It is best to start slow and build your confidence with racket familiarisation and close touch control before building in more power to your shots.

5949.statement: Pupils add their non dominant hand to the bottom of the grip when hitting backhands.
5949.correction: It is essential that your dominant racket hand is at the bottom of the grip and if you add your other hand for extra control or power it must go further up the racket shaft.

7894.belief: They have to hit the serve as hard as possible to be effective.
7894.statement: Pupils think they have to hit the serve as hard as possible to be effective.
7894.correction: Placement, spin and consistency are far more important when learning to serve.

8547.statement: Pupils use a big swing for volleys and consequently regularly miss the ball or hit it out.
8547.correction: When playing close to the net, you don't need to apply much swing and instead should use the power already in the ball, combined with a step into the shot, to apply power with more of a short punching action to block the ball back.

6377.statement: Pupils don't align their court positioning and often find themselves with one player forward and one back.
6377.correction: If one player is at the net and one is back on the baseline, it leaves big diagonal gaps through the court so it is essential for both be at net or both be on the baseline as much as possible.

5669.belief: Every point is equally important in tennis.
5669.statement: Every point is equally important in tennis.
5669.correction: Break point and other points to the advantage side are far more important to avoid losing a game on your own serve or winning/losing a game respectively. In the 2019 Wimbledon final, Federer won 14 more points than Djokovic, but lost the match.

5967.statement: Pupils may argue about decisions, particularly close calls such as run outs. This can often lead to the decision going in the favour of the more dominant or boisterous pupils.
5967.correction: Pupils should experience the umpire role to practise making fair decisions and develop empathy, helping them understand not to challenge calls.

7129.statement: Pupils may not always recognise that celebrating others' achievements is an important part of their own development and contribution to the team.
7129.correction: Encourage pupils that part of the game is to show respect and to respecfully physically appreciate it when someone performs well.

7556.statement: Pupils will swing the bat across their body like a baseball bat which increases the chance of missing the ball, edging it or getting out.
7556.correction: Pupils should understand that because of the way the ball is bowled in cricket, playing with a straight bat is often the most effective way to strike and not risk your wicket.

10999.belief: When wicket keeping, pupils have a tendency to stand right up to the wickets, no matter how fast the bowler is. This means they can't react quick enough to faster balls.
10999.statement: When wicket keeping, pupils have a tendency to stand right up to the wickets, no matter how fast the bowler is. This means they can't react quick enough to faster balls.
10999.correction: Pupils should understand that they can adjust the distance between wicket keeper and stumps, depending on the speed of the bowler, so they are catching the ball around thigh height. There is no standard wicket keeper position.

6072.belief: If they are not the fielder chasing a ball, they are not needed, even though the chasing fielder cannot throw the full distance to the wickets.
6072.statement: Pupils may believe that if they are not the fielder chasing a ball, they are not needed, even though the chasing fielder cannot throw the full distance to the wickets.
6072.correction: Pupils should understand that fielders need to work together and if they think the fielder will struggle to throw the distance, they should support by positioning themselves to relay the ball.

6379.statement: Some pupils don't consider the emotions of other people involved in a game which can lead to unsavoury comments after mistakes or poor play.
6379.correction: Encourage pupils to consider the emotions of others and how they might be able to positively influence the emotions of others through words and actions.

6047.belief: Benchmarking times represent their fixed ability and that their times won’t change.
6047.statement: Pupils might believe that benchmarking times represent their fixed ability and that their times won’t change.
6047.correction: Encourage pupils to understand that benchmarking is a snapshot in time - a starting point that effort and hard work can improve (growth mindset).

7485.statement: Pupils often struggle with setting a realistic goal for themselves, often have plans that are too ambitious for the time available or opportunity to train towards it.
7485.correction: Pupils should be aware that progress over several weeks can be marginal and that fitness gains take time and consistency. They can use the resources provided to help set realistic goals.

6086.belief: Improving at a physical activity requires them to perform the event in full repeatedly.
6086.statement: Pupils may believe that improving at a physical activity requires them to perform the event in full repeatedly.
6086.correction: Help pupils to understand that training drills which overload the body are much more effective when training to achieve a goal, rather than simply repeating the full performance.

8515.statement: Pupils may not understand the relationship between rest and workouts, believing that more training, equals more progress.
8515.correction: Help pupils to understand the requirement for sufficient rest and recovery time if the body is to make adaptations and improve.

6124.belief: Repeating the same drills every session is the best way to improve.
6124.statement: Pupils may believe that repeating the same drills every session is the best way to improve.
6124.correction: Even performing the best drills or exercise will become boring after time. Therefore variation is required in a training programme, otherwise it will become boring and the athlete will lose interest.

6096.belief: The longer your stride, the faster you'll run.
6096.statement: Pupils may believe that the longer your stride, the faster you'll run.
6096.correction: Thinking about stride length and experimenting with different lengths can help pupils to understand the optimal length of stride and its relationship with cadence.

8468.statement: Pupils may be unaware of the variety of training methods available to use for improving fitness and performance.
8468.correction: Continue to give pupils experiences which demonstrate different methods of training and ways to structure sessions, such as interval and plyometric training.

6204.statement: Pupils may compare their progress to other pupils and feel disappointed if others have made a faster rate of progress.
6204.correction: Progress is personal and depends on many things - starting fitness, goals, technique and even how well rested you are on test day. Even small amounts of progress should be celebrated.

6936.statement: Pupils often massively misjudge how much incremental overload can be achieved week on week.
6936.correction: Explain that small incremental increases in overload using the FITT principle will bring about results safely.

5618.belief: PNF can sometimes be confused as a partner simply helping to deepen the stretch by pushing a bit further.
5618.statement: PNF can sometimes be confused as a partner simply helping to deepen the stretch by pushing a bit further.
5618.correction: The method of contracting the muscle activates the nervous system which helps improve flexibility more effectively than static stretching alone.

6101.belief: They need to feel hyped up or overly energised to perform well.
6101.statement: Pupils may believe that they need to feel hyped up or overly energised to perform well.
6101.correction: Overexcitement can lead to mistakes, such as, starting too fast or losing focus. Controlled breathing and mental rehearsal help you stay calm, focused and perform more efficiently.

6097.belief: They can maintain their shorter distance pace over the longer distance, without needing to adjust.
6097.statement: Pupils often believe they can maintain their shorter distance pace over the longer distance, without needing to adjust.
6097.correction: Longer distances require more controlled pacing. Running a 1500m at 800m pace or a 200m at 100m pace will almost always lead to early fatigue and poor performance. Learning to distribute your effort is key to completing longer events effectively.

5855.belief: Progressive overload only applies when weight training.
5855.statement: Progressive overload only applies when weight training.
5855.correction: Gradually increasing frequency, intensity and time or altering the type of exercise through the manipulation of different training methods can develop all fitness components. Clear examples must be shared across activities other than weight training.

2955.belief: Feeling disappointed if some fitness test results fall below national average.
2955.statement: Feeling disappointed if some fitness test results fall below national average.
2955.correction: We all have different strengths and weaknesses and this is why we train to improve our areas of weakness.

2815.belief: Everyone needs exactly the same nutritional plan.
2815.statement: Everyone needs exactly the same nutritional plan.
2815.correction: Different people have different nutritional needs, at different times in life, especially when training for different activities.

5965.statement: Some pupils approach many fitness tasks as a race/competition and often give up as opposed to slowing down and maintaining movement until the end.
5965.correction: Reassure that a finishing position is irrelevant and instead focus on personal performance and improvement to their own fitness.

10971.belief: Weight training is only for people wanting to improve muscular strength.
10971.statement: Weight training is only for people wanting to improve muscular strength.
10971.correction: Weight training improves strength, muscular endurance, power and speed, as well as increasing bone density and joint stability while reducing the risk of injury.

3048.belief: Flexibility training is only for dancers or gymnasts.
3048.statement: Flexibility training is only for dancers or gymnasts.
3048.correction: Flexibility training is useful for all athletes as it can improve mobility, posture and reduce muscle tension making all movements easier.

7313.statement: Some pupils may struggle to believe the impact your mindset can have on performance.
7313.correction: Your mindset can be the difference between giving up and persisting, through the use of mindfulness, visualisation and positive self talk anything is possible.

8970.belief: Every risk can be planned for.
8970.statement: Every risk can be planned for.
8970.correction: There may be some risks that cannot be planned for, so we must be able to dynamically risk assess on an ongoing basis (e.g. the piece of equipment you were planning to use breaks and becomes unfit for purpose).

10532.belief: Underestimating the amount of water the body needs throughout the day (not just during exercise) to maintain hydration.
10532.statement: Underestimating the amount of water the body needs throughout the day (not just during exercise) to maintain hydration.
10532.correction: The general recommendation is 2 litres of water per day, however when training, more should be consumed.

10377.belief: Training a lot more will automatically improve your fitness.
10377.statement: Training a lot more will automatically improve your fitness.
10377.correction: Without adequate rest within a training programme, the individual will have a higher chance of injury, decreased performance and chronic fatigue.

2853.belief: Expecting progress to show huge improvements.
2853.statement: Expecting progress to show huge improvements.
2853.correction: different factors could affect the level of progress including frequency, effort, sleep and nutrition. Further training could show more improvement.

5854.belief: Progress will always be made at the same rate.
5854.statement: Progress will always be made at the same rate.
5854.correction: Sometimes different factors affect level of progress (sleep, hormones, nutrition) but also training results can plateau and changes to training are needed to continue to push the body to adapt.

6012.statement: Pupils attack one end of the court similar to all other invasion games focused on territory and seek to tackle/intercept passes between the opposition.
6012.correction: Tchoukball is a unique game where both teams can score at both ends by throwing the ball into the rebound net and not being caught by the opposition. You are not allowed to tackle with the opposition while they are in possession of the ball.

6930.statement: Pupils make simple ball handling mistakes due to rushing.
6930.correction: You lose possession if the ball is dropped, so whilst you need to make a pass within 3 seconds, it is essential not to make rushed decisions for passing and focus on catching the ball carefully with both hands before making your next move.

8582.statement: Pupils always use the same type of shot.
8582.correction: Just throwing the ball harder at the rebound frame increases the risk of a fault from failing to hit the target but is also very predictable for the opposition. Therefore vary your angle, speed and deception applied when shooting.

7759.belief: A defensive player must catch the ball outright on initial contact from a shot.
7759.statement: Pupils think a defensive player must catch the ball outright on initial contact from a shot.
7759.correction: It is sometimes more effective to bump a rebound up in the air for a teammate to catch, but it does then count as a pass. Whereas if you catch it cleanly or catch your own rebound, it doesn't use up one of your passes.

8583.statement: Pupils always use the same type of throw for passing and shooting (i.e. overarm with a focus on power and a direct route to the rebound frame).
8583.correction: It is easy to defend a square shot or an obvious attack angle at the rebound frame. To outwit the opposition, look to vary the type, angle and pace of shots as well as utilising fakes (e.g. a switch).

8245.belief: A short is associated with the height of a shot.
8245.statement: Pupils think a short is associated with the height of a shot.
8245.correction: A short is when a shot misses the rebound frame completely. It results in a fault and change of possession with the defenders restarting play from behind the baseline.

2506.belief: When dribbling the ball eyes should always be down looking at the ball.
2506.statement: When dribbling the ball eyes should always be down looking at the ball.
2506.correction: Whilst it's important to control the ball, always looking down means you can't see what's happening in the game. Keeping the head up improves decision-making, allowing players to see defenders, find passing options and spaces to dribble into.

8789.belief: When receiving the ball from the side, hitting to score is easy with the ball at the side.
8789.statement: When receiving the ball from the side, hitting to score is easy with the ball at the side.
8789.correction: It is easier to hit the ball with more power by controlling it and positoning it slightly to right and forward of your feet before hitting it. This allows a better angle for accuracy and power as the ball already has momentum towards the goal.

3891.belief: It's only the defenders that need to be good at tackling.
3891.statement: It's only the defenders that need to be good at tackling.
3891.correction: Tackling is a crucial skill for all players, not just defenders. Midfielders need to win possession and disrupt attacks, while forwards use tackling to press high up the pitch and regain the ball in attacking areas.

3329.belief: As a goalkeeper it is important to use your stick to hit away the ball.
3329.statement: As a goalkeeper it is important to use your stick to hit away the ball.
3329.correction: It's often more effective to rely on your pads or kickers for blocking low shots and redirecting the ball to safety. The stick is mainly for high / wide shots or controlling passes, but your legs and body provide a larger surface area for most shots.

4261.belief: Long corners are actually taken from the corner of the pitch.
4261.statement: Long corners are actually taken from the corner of the pitch.
4261.correction: Long corners are taken on the 23m line, in line with where the ball went out. They used to be taken from the corners, but the rule changed in 2015.

637.belief: It is best for lots of attackers to be near the ball so they have more chance of keeping possession.
637.statement: It is best for lots of attackers to be near the ball so they have more chance of keeping possession.
637.correction: Overcrowding the ball limits passing options, reduces space and makes it easier for defenders to win possession, so attackers should spread out to keep better control.

6155.belief: Twisting on the vertical axis is pointless as they are keen to do tricks which are often completed around the horizontal axis.
6155.statement: Pupils believe twisting on the vertical axis is pointless as they are keen to do tricks which are often completed around the horizontal axis.
6155.correction: Learning to twist is fundamental to overcome possible anxiety when in motion and not being able to see the cross. In addition, more challenging techniques include a twist at the start or the end, so the motor programme is required to build on this.

8033.belief: You need to drop backwards and/or lift the legs upwards to achieve a seated position.
8033.statement: Pupils think you need to drop backwards and/or lift the legs upwards to achieve a seated position.
8033.correction: This will lead to being off balance and not allow any progressions from the seat landing. The key to the correct technique is to avoid lifting the legs and jump upwards with a hinge at the hip to then land downwards.

8032.belief: You need to dive from a straight forward position to land in a front landing position.
8032.statement: Pupils think you need to dive from a straight forward position to land in a front landing position.
8032.correction: The hips should land in the same position as the take off for the front landing. This means the hips need to lift and move backwards slightly to initiate the forward movement.

8037.belief: You need to jump backwards to land in a back landing position.
8037.statement: Pupils think you need to jump backwards to land in a back landing position.
8037.correction: A back landing can feel quite scary. Jumping backwards can lead to injury and a back landing should only be attempted if your teacher has approved and is confident you will not jump backwards and will push the hips forwards when jumping upwards.

6093.belief: Landing a somersault is achieved through speed of rotation.
6093.statement: Pupils believe that landing a somersault is achieved through speed of rotation.
6093.correction: A somersault does require some speed, but if too much power is placed on the take off, it can lead to over rotation. A somersault will appear controlled with a balanced take off and the rebound of the trampoline initiating the hips for the rotation.

8113.belief: A performance of a 10 bounce routine has to include lots of difficult skills.
8113.statement: Pupils think a performance of a 10 bounce routine has to include lots of difficult skills.
8113.correction: There is judgement on difficulty through tariffs, however the performance is also linked to maintenance of height / execution with good technique. Often it is better to go simple with good execution, rather than difficult and have no control.

9350.belief: Sitting volleyball is only for people with disabilities.
9350.statement: Sitting volleyball is only for people with disabilities.
9350.correction: Sitting volleyball is a Paralympic sport, however it is an inclusive and adapted sport that anyone can play regardless of ability. Players have to move quickly around the court using their upper bodies frequently in a seated position.

8273.belief: A spike is performed with the hand in a fist shape.
8273.statement: Pupils think that a spike is performed with the hand in a fist shape.
8273.correction: A spike is performed with an open hand with the fingers together and the ball contacting the centre of the palm.

7678.belief: A bump shot needs the hands to come together to make a fist.
7678.statement: Pupils think a bump shot needs the hands to come together to make a fist.
7678.correction: The correct technique is to place the back of one hand in the palm of the other hand with the arms extended and the elbows locked creating a platform with the forearms.

8240.belief: Serving speed is the most important factor to an effective serve.
8240.statement: Pupils think serving speed is the most important factor to an effective serve.
8240.correction: The reality of a successful serve is placement and consistency.

8161.belief: A position in volleyball is determined by their physical location on the court.
8161.statement: Pupils think a position in volleyball is determined by their physical location on the court.
8161.correction: Rotations do occur based on court location but players are also assigned positions, with an assigned role, which they can move into directly after the serve.

2956.belief: The feet can not be used as a body part in volleyball.
2956.statement: The feet can not be used as a body part in volleyball.
2956.correction: Using the foot to contact the ball is legal but the foot must remain in contact with the ground. Players only tend to use this to slide the foot into the path of the ball as they simply cannot kick the ball.

6383.correction: Whilst no activity is attractive to everyone, most pupils enjoy dance when the tasks are open ended. This gives them the opportunity to input their own ideas and perform actions thay are comfortable with.

8560.belief: The pupils should only use ideas introduced by the teacher.
8560.statement: The pupils should only use ideas introduced by the teacher.
8560.correction: Cross curricular lessons offer scope for pupils to include additional content by bringing, sharing and consolidating subject knowledge from other curriculum areas. Enabling pupils to expand the action content will increase motivation and engagement.

3655.belief: It is important that the pupils listen to the music before beginning to choreograph their dances.
3655.statement: It is important that the pupils listen to the music before beginning to choreograph their dances.
3655.correction: Engaging pupils in the active content of the lesson is likely to improve motivation and levels of engagement. By playing the music in the background they will become familiar with it and allow it to inform the work they create.

2168.belief: Dancers should be moving all the time.
2168.statement: Dancers should be moving all the time.
2168.correction: Stillness is one of the five basic actions. Similar to punctuation in a sentence, it can help to bring meaning and context as well as highlight important moments. Stillness can include brief pauses as well as prolonged periods of inactivity.

8930.belief: Retrograde is a term only used in dance.
8930.statement: Retrograde is a term only used in dance.
8930.correction: Retrograde is a term used in many artforms, it is particularly prevalent in music and films.

5860.belief: Projection means that you have to look up.
5860.statement: Projection means that you have to look up.
5860.correction: Projection is effectively communicating a dance idea. This often involves looking outwards towards an audience but would not be appropriate if communicating a concept such a secrecy, nervousness or reluctance.

6686.statement: Pupils often forget to chant "Kabaddi Kabaddi" when they are a raider.
6686.correction: Remember chanting "Kabaddi, Kabaddi" is how the raider shows they haven't taken a breath during the raid and if they forget, the raid doesn't count.

7756.belief: As a defender they need to rush individually to stop the opposition.
7756.statement: Pupils think that as a defender they need to rush individually to stop the opposition.
7756.correction: Rushing alone often leaves space for the raider to escape. Defenders are more effective when they move together, stay connected and communicate to trap the raider as a team.

7590.belief: They have 6 'downs/tags' like tag rugby or rugby league.
7590.statement: Pupils think they have 6 'downs/tags' like tag rugby or rugby league.
7590.correction: In flag football, teams only have 4 downs (or attempts) to advance the ball 10 yards or score. If they don't succeed within those 4 downs, the ball is turned over to the other team.

7641.belief: The attacking players can block the blitzer so that the quarterback remains able to pass the ball.
7641.statement: Pupils think the attacking players can block the blitzer so that the quarterback remains able to pass the ball.
7641.correction: In flag football, blocking the blitzer is not allowed. Attackers must avoid physical contact and the quarterback must rely on quick throws and good timing to avoid being tagged by the blitzer.

8225.belief: They can run freely with the ball in Aussie rules.
8225.statement: Pupils may think they can run freely with the ball in Aussie rules.
8225.correction: In Aussie Rules, players must bounce or touch the ball to the ground every 15 metres when running with it. Running freely without doing so results in a turnover.

7294.statement: Pupils just stick with one payer on the opposite team and chase them.
7294.correction: The game moves too fast to just stick with 1 player, so it is better to work with teammates to create zonal defence.

4435.belief: For many pupils, softball may be a totally new game. It's a game with a lot of different rules from the striking and fielding games they will already know such as rounders and cricket.
4435.statement: For many pupils, softball may be a totally new game. It's a game with a lot of different rules from the striking and fielding games they will already know such as rounders and cricket.
4435.correction: Learning the intricacies, language and rules of the game in the first lesson and playing a version which includes most of the main rules, will allow pupils to relate to, and see sense in what they learn later in the unit, to the game itself.

8591.statement: Pupils may use a static approach to batting, perhaps using only their arms to swing the bat with.
8591.correction: Pupils should understand the whole body is involved in a good batting swing and that most of the power produced comes from the lower half of the body.

5982.belief: A fielder needs to be stationed on each base and that it is the job of other fielders to get the ball to them while they remain with their base.
5982.statement: Pupils often assume that a fielder needs to be stationed on each base and that it is the job of other fielders to get the ball to them while they remain with their base.
5982.correction: Use the third section of this lesson to introduce the idea that fielding positions should be fluid and that infielders, especially, should always be alert to the idea of leaving bases or covering other bases.

6465.statement: Pupils may field fly balls by putting their arm up in the air then running to where they think it'll land.
6465.correction: Teach pupils to beat the ball to the landing spot by running fast - something which can't be done with one arm in the air - then position themselves to catch.

7070.statement: Pupils often pay little attention to strategy and think only of themselves and not what the team needs. Many will only think of hitting the ball as hard and as far as they can.
7070.correction: Encourage pupils to consider team strategy, e.g. the batting line up based on strengths of the team. Stronger hitters bring others home and in some cases, a safe hit is much more useful to a team than trying to slog and getting caught or struck out.

6424.statement: Pupils who are more experienced may ignore the contribution of less able pupils, or even belittle or berate them when they don't contribute well to the team.
6424.correction: Encourage pupils to use their knowledge to offer feedback which can help bring about an improvement, emphasising that in team games, an individual cannot and should not perform all roles or carry the team.

10144.correction: Each stage of the challenge is possible. A reset in order to start again may be a good strategy if you get confused.

10551.belief: It is unsafe to be blindfolded.
10551.statement: It is unsafe to be blindfolded.
10551.correction: While there is an increased risk in getting injured, listening carefully to friends, trusting their guidance and being sensible will all help to reduce the risk level.

4479.belief: Matching a similar and incorrect photo as a result of rushing.
4479.statement: Matching a similar and incorrect photo as a result of rushing.
4479.correction: During photo orienteering, it is important to take your time and look at details carefully.

10338.belief: It is too tiring to sprint the whole course.
10338.statement: It is too tiring to sprint the whole course.
10338.correction: Strategise and plan who will take on what role and when to spread more difficult actions/moments among the team.

3016.correction: Accuracy and teamwork so we find the correct outcomes is more important than being first.

7835.belief: Fast running throughout will be the best pace to use in trail running.
7835.statement: Pupils think that fast running throughout will be the best pace to use in trail running.
7835.correction: Using smart pacing means the pupils can use variable speeds, across different terrain, to keep safe, save engery and complete the run.

3750.belief: Individual objects can't be used to make art.
3750.statement: Individual objects can't be used to make art.
3750.correction: If we collect a range of materials in contrasting colours and various textures, we can combine them to produce a nice composition.

8363.belief: Walking is boring and too easy.
8363.statement: Pupils may think that walking is boring and too easy.
8363.correction: Walking can be at different speeds, does not have to be boring and is a good opportunity to be present in the moment, which enhances positive mental health.

9293.belief: A simple or fast resolution is not always the best resolution.
9293.statement: A simple or fast resolution is not always the best resolution.
9293.correction: Sometimes deeper thinking is required to prevent further problems arising as a result of your actions.

3762.belief: Indoor caving is just about squeezing through tight spaces as quickly as possible.
3762.statement: Indoor caving is just about squeezing through tight spaces as quickly as possible.
3762.correction: Caving isn't just about speed. It involves planning, moving carefully, using spatial awareness and thinking ahead to create and navigate a route that is both enjoyable and challenging.

4893.belief: You need a strong throw to be good at darts.
4893.statement: You need a strong throw to be good at darts.
4893.correction: Darts is more about control and accuracy than power. A smooth, balanced stance and consistent release are more important.

231.belief: I am not a qualified first aider so I can't help someone in need.
231.statement: I am not a qualified first aider so I can't help someone in need.
231.correction: Basic knowledge can allow you to help with minor injuries. Knowing what to do in certain circumstances means that you can support and hopefully make a difference for any more major situations.

6466.statement: Pupils in fielding positions may lose focus when they are not involved for a spell of time and then miss an opportunity to field as a result.
6466.correction: Encourage pupils to communicate regularly and relay the ball back to the bowler via 1 or 2 fielders to keep everyone alert - e.g. the wicket keeper takes a catch, passes it to the slip fielder who sends it to another fielder and then to bowler.

8289.belief: Success in bowling only comes if the ball hits the stumps.
8289.statement: Some pupils will think that success in bowling only comes if the ball hits the stumps.
8289.correction: In some situations, hitting the stumps is desirable, i.e., bowl a batter out / trap them lbw / win a bowl-out. However, all lengths have their uses and a good bowler can pitch the ball at a wide range of different lengths.

4450.belief: Many young batters fail to move their feet when batting, instead they try to contort their bodies to deal with all sorts of line and length deliveries with little success.
4450.statement: Many young batters fail to move their feet when batting, instead they try to contort their bodies to deal with all sorts of line and length deliveries with little success.
4450.correction: Through practice, pupils can learn how to move their feet in response to different pitches of delivery. With short deliveries moving weight on to the back foot and changing foot position allows for pull, hook and cut shots.

905.belief: There is certainly a misconception with many pupils that the ball should be hit out into the field whenever possible, exacerbated by the need to do this in many other striking and fielding games.
905.statement: There is certainly a misconception with many pupils that the ball should be hit out into the field whenever possible, exacerbated by the need to do this in many other striking and fielding games.
905.correction: Pupils should understand on occasions in cricket, blocking or leaving the ball are actually preferable shots to play, rather than shots with a higher risk of getting out. It requires a different mindset to a lot of other striking and fielding games.

1824.belief: Communication after the ball is hit can be inconsistent in cricket. Having four players to coordinate means the need to communicate clearly about how many runs to make is even more important.
1824.statement: Communication after the ball is hit can be inconsistent in cricket. Having four players to coordinate means the need to communicate clearly about how many runs to make is even more important.
1824.correction: Allow pupils time to strategise about how they will communicate after the ball is hit. For example, they may nominate a captain to make all calls or decide that the batter who hit the ball makes the call.

4430.belief: Many pupils do not consider how adaptations and conditions can make games more enjoyable for different people, preferring to play the full version of a game even when it might be a struggle.
4430.statement: Many pupils do not consider how adaptations and conditions can make games more enjoyable for different people, preferring to play the full version of a game even when it might be a struggle.
4430.correction: Helping pupils to be conscious of other people's motivations and understand how adaptations can make the game more accessible and enjoyable.

7292.statement: Pupils stay upright while kneeling in the tripod position, meaning the ball is too high for hitting.
7292.correction: It is easier to hit the kin-ball when it is lower down, so be sure to bend forward in the kneeling position.

3952.belief: The kin-ball is light as it is full of air and travels slowly so it doesn't require much strength.
3952.statement: The kin-ball is light as it is full of air and travels slowly so it doesn't require much strength.
3952.correction: When the kin-ball is dropping to the floor, trying to stop it with outstretched arms takes significant effort and core strength.

5919.belief: Punching is an effective way of hitting the kin-ball.
5919.statement: Punching is an effective way of hitting the kin-ball.
5919.correction: Hitting with your hands clasped together helps to prevent injury, improve stability, ensure accuracy and enable faster, stronger hits.

3948.belief: Kicking the kin-ball on its side, similar to kicking a football, is considered an effective strategy.
3948.statement: Kicking the kin-ball on its side, similar to kicking a football, is considered an effective strategy.
3948.correction: It is important to kick the kin-ball on the underside of the ball to help reduce the risk of injury and maximise the chances of gaining height and therefore keeping it off the floor.

6551.statement: Pupils find it difficult to get into an effective defensive position.
6551.correction: A quick transition out of a set position will reduce the chance of this occuring.

10154.belief: A team hit the kin-ball without properly nominating a team to defend.
10154.statement: A team hit the kin-ball without properly nominating a team to defend.
10154.correction: Each hitting team must shout "Omnikin" followed by the colour of the bib worn by the nominated team before hitting the kin-ball.

8034.belief: You need to be a good tennis player to participate in cardio tennis.
8034.statement: Pupils think you need to be a good tennis player to participate in cardio tennis.
8034.correction: The focus is on the workout rather than the execution of shots. It is about having fun while exercising. You should prioritise keeping your heart rate elevated for the whole lesson rather than great shots or winning rallies.

7648.belief: Balance is only a static position, such as standing on one leg, and is only really needed in sports like gymnastics.
7648.statement: Pupils think balance is only a static position, such as standing on one leg, and is only really needed in sports like gymnastics.
7648.correction: The ability to balance whilst static is essential in sport and in life, be that on one leg or two, but it is important to highlight the kinaesthetic awareness that unlocks success is also required in dynamic balances (i.e. while on the move).

8166.belief: Power comes from just the size and strength of muscles.
8166.statement: Pupils think power comes from just the size and strength of muscles.
8166.correction: Strength is important to generate power but so are speed, timing, coordination and the combination of levers to transfer power up from the ground.

7737.belief: It is not cool to sweat or that it shows they are working too hard or are unfit.
7737.statement: Pupils think it is not cool to sweat or that it shows they are working too hard or are unfit.
7737.correction: The sweating response is essential to homeostasis and keeping your core body temperature stable. An increased sweating response is actually an indicator of better aerobic fitness and is required when seeking a cardiovascular benefit from training.

6190.statement: Pupils choose to play with one player at the net and their partner at the back of the court.
6190.correction: Splitting front and back leaves a huge gap diagonally through your court that the opposition can exploit.

6764.statement: Pupils give up when training gets tough rather than pushing themselves closer to exhaustion.
6764.correction: To get a fitness benefit, it is essential to work your body harder than it is used to and hence a little discomfort is necessary to improve. This is often referred to as no pain, no gain.

2510.belief: When dribbling, you should always be looking at the ball in order to maintain control.
2510.statement: When dribbling, you should always be looking at the ball in order to maintain control.
2510.correction: When dribbling, it is important to look up to see your surroundings, any opposition and where the space is.

2505.belief: You can only dribble with your hands or feet.
2505.statement: You can only dribble with your hands or feet.
2505.correction: You can also use an implement to dribble with.

2610.belief: You are either naturally good at movement skills and sports, or you aren't.
2610.statement: You are either naturally good at movement skills and sports, or you aren't.
2610.correction: Movement skills are learned and trained, just like maths and music. You need to practice and refine your technique to improve confidence and remember that growth spurts will temporarily affect coordination and this is perfectly normal.

3342.belief: Being good at sport just means being fast or strong.
3342.statement: Being good at sport just means being fast or strong.
3342.correction: Success in sport depends on coordination and balance, timing and decision making, technique and skill execution, awareness of space and teammates, and many other factors including experience. Many of these can be practised away from the sports pitch.

656.correction: Sometimes more subtle, small emotions can be expressive in how they portray emotions.

3680.belief: Improvising can have a negative effect on a dance sequence.
3680.statement: Improvising can have a negative effect on a dance sequence.
3680.correction: Improvising is actually a useful way to explore ideas, express emotions and develop new movements. It allows dancers to be creative and adapt their sequence, which can make the dance more interesting and personal.

1858.belief: A compass is only needed outside.
1858.statement: A compass is only needed outside.
1858.correction: A compass can be used anywhere to help us gain an understanding of direction.

4884.belief: You need a properly mapped area to be able to participate in orienteering.
4884.statement: You need a properly mapped area to be able to participate in orienteering.
4884.correction: You can use an image from google maps or your own drawn map and still be able to participate in orienteering fully.

4500.belief: Maximum repetitions is the highest priority in body weight exercises.
4500.statement: Maximum repetitions is the highest priority in body weight exercises.
4500.correction: Ensuring every exercise is completed with the correct technique to avoid injury and through the full range of movement is more important than the total repetitions.

10374.belief: Training abdominals for a 6 pack but neglecting other core muscles.
10374.statement: Training abdominals for a 6 pack but neglecting other core muscles.
10374.correction: It is essential to balance training on all core muscles to maintain good posture, alignment and strength on anterior and posterior sides of the body.

4674.belief: Mixing up the different body systems and terminology used for each (for example, not realising the cardio-respiratory system refers to the heart and lungs).
4674.statement: Mixing up the different body systems and terminology used for each (for example, not realising the cardio-respiratory system refers to the heart and lungs).
4674.correction: Ensure pupils understand that muscular means muscles, skeletal means bones, cardio means heart, vascular means blood vessels and respiratory means lungs.

4226.belief: Little bones in the hand and foot are not considered long bones.
4226.statement: Little bones in the hand and foot are not considered long bones.
4226.correction: Bones are classified based on their shape, if the shaft is longer than than the width and depth of a bone, it is referred to as a long bone even if it is small in size.

1959.belief: There can be confusion between the role of ligaments and tendons.
1959.statement: There can be confusion between the role of ligaments and tendons.
1959.correction: Ligaments connect bone to bone to stabilise a joint whereas tendons attach muscle to bone to enable movement.

9777.statement: Students may mix up rotation and circumduction.
9777.correction: When you rotate the shoulder joint you draw a dot with your hand (if the elbow is fully extended) whereas circumduction draws a circle.

4765.correction: Muscles are only able to pull, they work in antagonistic pairs so one muscle can contract to create a movement whilst the other relaxes in opposition and then their roles are reversed to move back.

4764.belief: A muscle will always change length when it contracts.
4764.statement: A muscle will always change length when it contracts.
4764.correction: A muscle pulls on a bone to create movement. However, occasionally, if the movement is static, the muscle is still contracting and under tension but not changing length. This is known as isometric muscle contraction.

9276.belief: Which side of the heart is the left when you look at the body and which side is oxygenated versus deoxygenated.
9276.statement: Which side of the heart is the left when you look at the body and which side is oxygenated versus deoxygenated.
9276.correction: The left side of the heart is nearest your left armpit and carries oxygenated blood, the right side of the heart has deoxygenated blood (remember: LORD - left, oxygenated and right, deogygenated).

403.correction: The pulmonary artery is the only artery in the body that carries deoxygenated blood as it is pumped back to the lungs to be re-oxygenated. Consequently, the pulmonary vein is the only vein in the body that carries oxygenated blood.

7762.belief: Deoxygenated blood at the muscle tissue goes straight to the lungs rather than via the heart first (i.e. they forget they need to go through the heart twice).
7762.statement: Pupils think deoxygenated blood at the muscle tissue goes straight to the lungs rather than via the heart first (i.e. they forget they need to go through the heart twice).
7762.correction: Remind pupils the heart is a double circulatory pump consisting of a pulmonary and a systemic loop. Without this, blood pressure would be too low on return from the legs to efficiently get blood to the lungs for oxygenation.

521.belief: The ba-dum of the heart beat represents the left then right side contracting.
521.statement: The ba-dum of the heart beat represents the left then right side contracting.
521.correction: The heart relaxes (diastole) to fill with blood then first phase of contraction squeezes blood from the top two atria down into the ventricles before the valves close off and then the second phase of contraction squeezes blood out of the ventricles.

6393.statement: Pupils often draw heart rate down to zero on a line graph.
6393.correction: Even at rest your heart is still beating, on average 72 beats per minute, to ensure blood is always circulating around the body to keep you alive.

3214.correction: Gaseous exchange is when oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse between the lungs and the blood, and then between the blood and muscle tissues.

5289.belief: All of the oxygen we breathe in is used by the muscles.
5289.statement: All of the oxygen we breathe in is used by the muscles.
5289.correction: The body only extracts a small percentage of the oxygen in each breath so it is important we keep breathing during and after exercise. You can only moves gases to an area of lower concentration so once that is equal diffusion stops.

10321.belief: Tidal volume is the amount of air breathed in and out per breath and the lungs completely empty of air when we expire.
10321.statement: Tidal volume is the amount of air breathed in and out per breath and the lungs completely empty of air when we expire.
10321.correction: Tidal volume is the volume of air breathed in or out per breadth and it increases during exercise to enable more air and hence exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide to occur. A residual volume of air always remains in the lungs to keep them inflated.

8537.statement: Pupils are unsure about situations when the body works aerobically and when it works anaerobically.
8537.correction: Aerobic exercise requires oxygen from the air we breathe to totally break down glucose to release energy for exercise. This is the most efficient mechanism but requires exercise to be at a low/ moderate intensity, whereas high intensity is anaerobic.

2041.belief: A cool down will always prevent DOMS.
2041.statement: A cool down will always prevent DOMS.
2041.correction: An active cool down supports better recovery from exercise by prolonging elevated heart and breathing rates to flush fresh oxygen through the muscles, but small micro tears in the muscles may still result in soreness 24-48 hours after exercise.

4676.belief: Mixing up immediate, short-term and long-term effects of exercise.
4676.statement: Mixing up immediate, short-term and long-term effects of exercise.
4676.correction: Immediate effects are what happens as soon as we start exercising to cope with it, whereas short-term effects are those that happen over the next 36 hours. Long-term refers to the adaptations that happen in response to training.

5879.belief: A proper cool down speeds up reduction in heart rate after exercise and prevents muscle soreness.
5879.statement: A proper cool down speeds up reduction in heart rate after exercise and prevents muscle soreness.
5879.correction: An active cool down actually prolongs the elevated heart and breathing rate after exercise to help flush fresh oxygen through the muscles and improve recovery. However, DOMS may still occur due to microtears in muscles if training was intense.

867.belief: Cardiorespiratory benefits only come from endurance training and muscle growth only comes from weight training.
867.statement: Cardiorespiratory benefits only come from endurance training and muscle growth only comes from weight training.
867.correction: Any training that regularly puts the bodily systems under more strain than they are in normal life, will lead to long term benefits to the muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems. However, training intensity will effect results.

2494.belief: When drawing levers, the body part needs to be included.
2494.statement: When drawing levers, the body part needs to be included.
2494.correction: A lever will always be drawn using four shapes.

2604.belief: The effort in a lever starts in the belly of the muscle.
2604.statement: The effort in a lever starts in the belly of the muscle.
2604.correction: The effort from a muscle will start from the muscle insertion. The insertion is the tendon attached to the bone which that muscle moves.

10416.belief: The transverse plane is linked with the transverse axis.
10416.statement: The transverse plane is linked with the transverse axis.
10416.correction: They share the same name, however the transverse plane is linked with the longitudinal axis. The transverse axis is linked with the sagittal plane. The frontal plane and axis however have the same name and are linked.

10308.belief: Any of the three planes can be paired with the three axes.
10308.statement: Any of the three planes can be paired with the three axes.
10308.correction: Planes and axes are always paired as; sagittal plane with the transverse axis, frontal plane with the sagittal axis and transverse plane with the longitudinal axis.

10294.belief: Being physically fit means that someone is healthy.
10294.statement: Thinking that being physically fit means that someone is healthy.
10294.correction: It is possible to be physically fit but unhealthy. It is essential to consider social and emotional benefits/aspects of health as well as strength, cardiovascular endurance etc.

9551.belief: Speed is just about running fast.
9551.statement: Speed is just about running fast.
9551.correction: An example of speed is moving quickly across the ground but also includes other body parts too such as the speed of arms in table tennis.

5169.belief: There is only one type of strength which we usually associate with lifting heavy weights.
5169.statement: There is only one type of strength which we usually associate with lifting heavy weights.
5169.correction: There are four types of strength: maximal, dynamic, static and explosive.

10280.belief: Flexibility is only useful for gymnasts or dancers.
10280.statement: Thinking that flexibility is only useful for gymnasts or dancers.
10280.correction: Discuss wider examples such as hurdlers, footballers and swimmers that will also benefit from high levels of flexibility.

9597.belief: Starting the multi stage fitness test too quickly.
9597.statement: Starting the multi stage fitness test too quickly.
9597.correction: It can be beneficial to start the multi stage fitness test at fast walking pace to conserve energy for the faster levels.

8749.belief: Raising the knees in the sit and reach test.
8749.statement: Raising the knees in the sit and reach test.
8749.correction: When performing the sit and reach test, the knees should be flat along the floor to give an accurate reading of flexibility.

1922.belief: When conducting the ruler drop test, the partner or assistant will countdown so the performer knows when the ruler is going to be dropped.
1922.statement: When conducting the ruler drop test, the partner or assistant will countdown so the performer knows when the ruler is going to be dropped.
1922.correction: Remind students that they need to drop the ruler randomly, rather than when the performer knows they will drop it, to really ensure validity to test reaction time.

9974.statement: Students thinking that certain sports only need one type of component of fitness to be successful e.g. 100m sprinter just needs speed.
9974.correction: Identify all the components of fitness that are useful for each athlete, determining why they are beneficial and justifying which is most important.

3038.belief: Fitness testing brings about improvements in components of fitness.
3038.statement: Fitness testing brings about improvements in components of fitness.
3038.correction: Training methods bring about improvement in fitness. Fitness testing is merely about identifying the strengths and weaknesses of a fitness component so the right training method can be allocated and used.

5287.belief: Overload is negative and should not be encouraged during training.
5287.statement: Overload is negative and should not be encouraged during training.
5287.correction: Overload is encouarged as a positive aspect of traning as progression is being managed correctly to bring about adaptations to fitness. It is not to be confused with 'overtraining' which can cause injuries.

4043.belief: The last two T's of the FITT acronym are interchangeable.
4043.statement: The last two T's of the FITT acronym are interchangeable.
4043.correction: The principle is set and the first 'T' references the time used to train and the second 'T' references the specific type of training method chosen to achieve the optimal fitness gains.

10376.belief: Training at the highest intensity is the best way to see results.
10376.statement: Training at the highest intensity is the best way to see results.
10376.correction: A balanced and accurate approach to training intensity using approximate zones is necessary to optimise fitness, recovery and avoid injury.

9563.belief: Each sport or activity has only one type of training suited to it.
9563.statement: Each sport or activity has only one type of training suited to it.
9563.correction: Performers in most activities can benefit from a range of training types. A marathon runner would benefit most from continuous training; however, weight training and static stretching would also help with conditioning and avoiding injury.

9040.belief: Running is the only type of interval training.
9040.statement: Running is the only type of interval training.
9040.correction: Interval training can be done with any activity as long as it involves high intesity work followed by a rest period.

8926.belief: Rest is not incorporated into these types of training.
8926.statement: That rest is not incorporated into these types of training.
8926.correction: All of these can be performed as a type of interval training and rest after each exercise / session is important to avoid the body getting injured.

10375.belief: Training at high altitude leads to permanent change in the body to support performance of an endurance athlete.
10375.statement: Training at high altitude leads to permanent change in the body to support performance of an endurance athlete.
10375.correction: Adaptations to altitude are lost very quickly when returning to sea level. Therefore, an endurance athlete needs to plan carefully when to access altitude to be at optimal performance.

10380.belief: Training seasons align with seasons of the year.
10380.statement: Training seasons align with seasons of the year.
10380.correction: They are very different. Training seasons will align with the type of sport and their competition period. For example, the football season is currently a different time period to the netball super league and hence their seasons will be set by this.

3795.belief: Injury prevention means injuries will not occur.
3795.statement: Injury prevention means injuries will not occur.
3795.correction: Nothing can guarantee that injuries will not happen, however the measures discussed in this lesson will significantly reduce the risk of injury. With the best prevention measures in place, accidents may still happen.

9644.belief: Stretching is the first part of a warm up routine.
9644.statement: Stretching is the first part of a warm up routine.
9644.correction: Before a muscle can be stretched it needs to have an increase in temperature and pliability. Therefore, before stretching, an individual should do a pulse raiser to increase blood flow to the muscles.

3381.belief: Graphs in exam questions will have the x and y axes labelled.
3381.statement: Graphs in exam questions will have the x and y axes labelled.
3381.correction: One of the skills assessed in GCSE PE exam questions is to label the x and y axes, as well as plot data and present as the method requested by the question.

243.belief: To analyse data you just need to explain what the data is demonstrating.
243.statement: To analyse data you just need to explain what the data is demonstrating.
243.correction: The analysis skill goes a little further and looks at patterns / trends / relationships in the context of data provided.

3687.belief: I must include fitness test protocols and scores to show my fitness strength and weakness.
3687.statement: I must include fitness test protocols and scores to show my fitness strength and weakness.
