3687.correction: This is not a requirement. The analysis of the fitness components is using recent competitive performances, and justifying how it benefited or negatively affected that actual performance/s.

596.belief: At the beginning of a sprint performance, pupils will rise up into an upright position as soon as possible.
596.statement: At the beginning of a sprint performance, pupils will rise up into an upright position as soon as possible.
596.correction: An effective drive phase of sprinting sees the body gradually rise up over the first 20m before assuming an upright position. Trying to get upright too soon after starting will hinder acceleration.

8422.statement: Pupils will tire during the latter phases of a 100m sprint race and may withdraw their effort because fatigue is setting in and they expected to perform at maximal throughout.
8422.correction: Fatigue will always feature in the final stages if the athlete is giving it their best. Recognising this by remaining determined to finish and maintaining technique will result in the best possible time.

7074.statement: Pupils may perform middle distances by jogging the majority to conserve energy and putting a sprint in at the end. This often leads to pupils wishing they had put more effort into the initial stages.
7074.correction: A well performed 800m requires a fine line between holding back some energy for the finish but also performing at around 80-90% maximum effort for around the first 600m.

6422.statement: Pupils expend far too much energy by sprint starting instead of finding their race pace, leading them to tire in the second half of the race.
6422.correction: Pupils should focus on finding their race pace, not getting over excited at the start line, beginning too fast or being influenced by others who do. Ideally, the second half of the race is completed quicker than the first (called a negative split).

6138.belief: Starting their approach from the furthest point on the runway will result in the best possible approach and jump.
6138.statement: Pupils believe starting their approach from the furthest point on the runway will result in the best possible approach and jump.
6138.correction: The approach is personalised and should be measured to ensure optimal speed is reached and the take off is smooth without the need to break stride. For most, the end of the runway will not be the ideal starting point.

6428.statement: Pupils often fail to get enough distance in the middle step phase of the triple jump and it is much shorter then the other two phases causing them to lose distance.
6428.correction: Help pupils to understand that ideally the distance covered in each phase will be similar. It might seem counterintuitive but the short step is often due to the hop stage being too long and we need to seek balance between all three stages.

7560.statement: Pupils take an approach straight towards the bar which is not conducive to performing the Fosbury flop technique and maximising height jumped.
7560.correction: Pupils should take a curved run up which is J-shaped and will allow them to perform the technique required to gain the most height in their jump. The teacher can guide them to this through the activities.

8419.statement: Pupils often throw the shot by leading with the elbow rather than push it with the elbow following behind the shot, which can sometimes lead to pain and injury, especially to the wrist.
8419.correction: Emphasise the need to push the shot by extending the arm and not trying to bring the shot behind the head to throw. Replace shot with lighter weighted balls (medicine) if necessary to avoid injury while the technique is being learned.

6767.statement: Pupils will grip the discus by wrapping their fingers and thumb around the edges to prevent it from slipping out or dropping it.
6767.correction: The discus should sit on the palm of the hand with the edge of the discus sitting in the last joint crease of the fingers (if you turn the hand over to the top, it should fall out). The thumb should not grip the edge at all.

544.belief: Ball control is mainly about dribbling.
544.statement: Ball control is mainly about dribbling.
544.correction: Control of the ball is the fundamental skill that is the basis of other skills such as dribbling, passing or shooting. With good ball control comes an increased opportunity to maintain possession of the ball.

7864.belief: GCSE assessment for passing is just looking at the techniques in isolation.
7864.statement: Pupils think that GCSE assessment for passing is just looking at the techniques in isolation.
7864.correction: Passing needs to be seen in progressive and conditioned practices to showcase the technique when faced with opposition and decision making.

5719.belief: Position of the non striking foot changes depending on where the shot is being aimed in the goal.
5719.statement: Position of the non striking foot changes depending on where the shot is being aimed in the goal.
5719.correction: This is a common myth, however the positioning of the non striking foot remains consistent and needs to be at the side of the ball for optimal balance and accuracy so the shot is precise and on target.

7863.belief: GCSE assessment for ball control is just looking at the techniques in isolation or in a 1v1.
7863.statement: Pupils think that GCSE assessment for ball control is just looking at the techniques in isolation or in a 1v1.
7863.correction: Dribbling and 1v1 needs to be seen in conditioned practices to showcase the technique when faced with the position of the defenders and decision making.

7758.belief: Defending is only important when playing a defensive position or during set pieces.
7758.statement: Pupils think that defending is only important when playing a defensive position or during set pieces.
7758.correction: Defence starts from the striker position and works all the back to the GK. Defending well as an individual leads to collective marking and reduction of attacking space and opportunities.

3216.belief: In a GCSE assessment the assessor will expect to see you be on the ball as an attacker and trying to beat defenders with tricks and feints.
3216.statement: In a GCSE assessment the assessor will expect to see you be on the ball as an attacker and trying to beat defenders with tricks and feints.
3216.correction: An assessor is looking for the selection of the most appropriate skill for the situation to outwit an opponent which could be a passing option or creating space. It is more about the contribution to the team performance and strategic application.

5589.belief: A player has to pivot as part of footwork to create space after landing when the ball has been caught.
5589.statement: A player has to pivot as part of footwork to create space after landing when the ball has been caught.
5589.correction: Although a pivot may be needed to create space and is permitted, it is better to turn in the air when reveiving the ball so landing is the right position for the next pass.

2442.belief: A dodge from a static position is a good place to showcase a dodge in isolation.
2442.statement: A dodge from a static position is a good place to showcase a dodge in isolation.
2442.correction: In game play, it is encouraged to be active and on the toes and thinking about a prelim movement before a change of direction or speed can be executed therefore encouraging this in early drills is advised.

6845.statement: Pupils keep their feet planted on the ground after taking a shot.
6845.correction: Always encourage a release of a shot, moving up onto the toes, so the player is in a suitable position to move forward for a rebound.

2211.belief: Each defender can only mark 1 attacker.
2211.statement: Each defender can only mark 1 attacker.
2211.correction: Netball positions are paired, however the competitive situation will determine if players swap, if they double mark and which stage of defence they need at that point.

5383.belief: When a penalty pass is awarded, the player infringed has to take the pass.
5383.statement: When a penalty pass is awarded, the player infringed has to take the pass.
5383.correction: Any player can take the penalty pass if it is in a third they are permitted to go into. Players need to communicate who this player can be in order to create an attacking advantage, as the player who made the infringement has to stand out of play.

5098.belief: Once a player has released the ball, the defenders' work is done.
5098.statement: Once a player has released the ball, the defenders' work is done.
5098.correction: Stage 3 defending can be used to impact the next phase of play.

640.belief: The best thing to do when a defender is about to tackle you is to (panic) pass the ball.
640.statement: The best thing to do when a defender is about to tackle you is to (panic) pass the ball.
640.correction: Panic passing before contact in rugby often leads to turnovers, as the pass is rushed, inaccurate, and easier for the opposition to intercept or disrupt, therefore the best decision can sometimes be to keep hold of the ball and take it into contact.

9557.belief: Spin passes are always better to use.
9557.statement: Spin passes are always better to use.
9557.correction: Short or soft pop passes can be more effective for quick, controlled distribution, especially in close quarters or wet conditions where accuracy and catchability matter more than speed.

9038.belief: Just running a hard straight line is the only way to evade defenders and break the line.
9038.statement: Just running a hard straight line is the only way to evade defenders and break the line.
9038.correction: While running a hard straight line can be effective, varying angles like overs and unders lines, footwork, and deception through dummying, are also crucial for evading defenders and breaking the line.

9039.belief: Running up quickly to tackle the ball carrier is always the best thing to do.
9039.statement: Running up quickly to tackle the ball carrier is always the best thing to do.
9039.correction: Moving up quickly to tackle the ball carrier is only the right thing to do if the rest of your defensive line is with you, as you can leave gaps which makes it easy for the ball carrier to stop you and break up the pitch to score a try.

9029.belief: In a rugby scrum you have to push (like in union).
9029.statement: In a rugby scrum you have to push (like in union).
9029.correction: Because the scrum half can throw the ball in at angle that is advantageous to their team, there is not much point pushing. It's better to save energy to get back to defend but if the other side are being lazy, it might be beneficial to push.

4306.belief: Losing a game will affect your GCSE PE moderation score.
4306.statement: Losing a game will affect your GCSE PE moderation score.
4306.correction: For your GCSE PE moderation, you are measured against how well you can demonstrate certain skills, tactics and decision making, not the final score of your game.

3736.belief: Having index finger up the back of the racket to try to control the racket in a pan handled grip.
3736.statement: Having index finger up the back of the racket to try to control the racket in a pan handled grip.
3736.correction: Ensure all fingers are wrapped in a shake hands grip to unlock the ability to hit with more power even if it feels harder initially. Watch out for others making this mistake with their grip and correct them when you see it.

3297.belief: Getting out of position after hitting a shot.
3297.statement: Getting out of position after hitting a shot.
3297.correction: Learning to lunge and recover quickly to the middle of the court requires explosive strength/power but avoids exposing space for your opposition to attack.

3514.belief: Hitting it hard and fast is the highest priority.
3514.statement: Hitting it hard and fast is the highest priority.
3514.correction: It is more effective to vary the pace, angle and positioning of where you hit the shuttle to create opportunities to win the point.

2517.belief: Drop shots and net shots are two terms for the same thing.
2517.statement: Drop shots and net shots are two terms for the same thing.
2517.correction: Whilst both shots play the shuttle just over the net, a drop shot is hit from the back of the court whereas a net shot is hit from the front of the court close to the net.

2750.belief: It is essential to attack at all times.
2750.statement: It is essential to attack at all times.
2750.correction: Often it can be just as effective to consistently get the shuttle back into play, keeping the shuttle in and forcing your opposition to make mistakes by varying pace and placement on the court.

168.belief: There is no advantage to delaying your shot when playing a compeititve game.
168.statement: There is no advantage to delaying your shot when playing a compeititve game.
168.correction: Delaying your shot can be effective at wrong footing your opponent.

5749.belief: Power is more important than accuracy.
5749.statement: Power is more important than accuracy.
5749.correction: Accuracy is crucial to keep the ball within possession of your team so you have more opportunities to score.

2508.belief: Dribbling is always the best option to move with the ball.
2508.statement: Dribbling is always the best option to move with the ball.
2508.correction: While dribbling can be helpful to gain ground up the court, it can slow down the game, whereas passing can often be faster and more efficient at breaking through a defence.

5591.belief: Players are not allowed in the D apart from the goalkeeper.
5591.statement: Players are not allowed in the D apart from the goalkeeper.
5591.correction: If you land in the goal area (the D) after taking a shot, the goal will still count as long as the ball was released before you entered the area. However, if you enter the goal area during regular play, possession is awarded to the opposing team.

9135.belief: Screening is a defensive move only used to stop the team with the ball scoring.
9135.statement: Screening is a defensive move only used to stop the team with the ball scoring.
9135.correction: Screening can be used by attackers to 'screen' or block defenders to allow an attacking teammate more space to move or score.

492.belief: When attacking, it is always best to just dribble or step and pass the ball straight up the court.
492.statement: When attacking, it is always best to just dribble or step and pass the ball straight up the court.
492.correction: Sometimes to create more space, a flat pass across the width of the pitch or a crossover move can be used to spread, reposition or confuse defenders which can be more successful at enabling a teammate to get through the gap that is created and score.

4307.belief: If you are on the losing team, it automatically affects the score you get for your handball assessment.
4307.statement: If you are on the losing team, it automatically affects the score you get for your handball assessment.
4307.correction: For your GCSE PE moderation, you are measured against how well you can demonstrate certain skills, tactics and decision making, not the final score of your game.

7662.belief: The best thing to do when a defender is about to tackle you is to (panic) pass the ball.
7662.statement: Pupils think the best thing to do when a defender is about to tackle you is to (panic) pass the ball.
7662.correction: Panic passing before contact in rugby often leads to turnovers, as the pass is rushed, inaccurate, and easier for the opposition to intercept or disrupt, therefore the best decision can sometimes be to keep hold of the ball and take it into contact.

8274.belief: Spin passes are always better to use.
8274.statement: Pupils think that spin passes are always better to use.
8274.correction: Short or soft pop passes can be more effective for quick, controlled distribution, especially in close quarters or wet conditions where accuracy and catchability matter more than speed.

8278.belief: They should stand next to the ball carrier when running a support line.
8278.statement: Pupils think they should stand next to the ball carrier when running a support line.
8278.correction: It is better to start deeper so you are able to catch the ball at full pace and have more chance of breaking the gain line

6427.statement: Pupils fail to fully commit to a tackle which allows players to break free and score.
6427.correction: Defenders must fully commit to tackle the ball carrier and keep hold until they are on the ground to avoid giving the opposition an overlap or charge through scoring opportunity.

5234.belief: In order to get the highest marks in GCSE PE moderation I need to be very good at all the specialist skills in rugby.
5234.statement: In order to get the highest marks in GCSE PE moderation I need to be very good at all the specialist skills in rugby.
5234.correction: Rugby allows for different body shapes that suit specific positions, meaning players do not need to master every specialist skill. Forwards focus on scrums, lineouts and physical contests, while backs excel in speed, passing and kicking.

8020.belief: They can move with the ball more than 2 steps before starting to dribble.
8020.statement: Pupils think they can move with the ball more than 2 steps before starting to dribble.
8020.correction: This can be seen at the elite level but will break the travelling rule.

7865.belief: For GCSE assessment, shooting is only required in isolation to demonstrate the correct techniques.
7865.statement: Pupils think that for GCSE assessment, shooting is only required in isolation to demonstrate the correct techniques.
7865.correction: Shooting needs to be seen in progressive and conditioned practices to showcase the technique when faced with decision making. The assessment will be based on the choice of shot or drive to the basket depending on the position of the defenders.

7755.belief: Defence is a solo effort and only needed when marking the player with the ball.
7755.statement: Pupils think defence is a solo effort and only needed when marking the player with the ball.
7755.correction: Individual defensive skills are crucial, however defending as a cohesive unit leads to the attacking team being denied space and vision to move the ball.

8122.belief: They are not permitted to jump on a free throw.
8122.statement: Pupils think they are not permitted to jump on a free throw.
8122.correction: There is no rule stating a jump is not permitted, however the feet can not pass the free throw line so players chose to keep their feet planted on the ground.

7866.belief: For GCSE assessment. their defence is looked at individually.
7866.statement: Pupils think that for GCSE assessment. their defence is looked at individually.
7866.correction: In the fully competitive game, part of the assessment is showing an understanding of the different types of defence and which would is best to use depending on the situation of the game.

6737.statement: Pupils may get confused with the different names of fast/ slow and type I/ type II muscle fibres.
6737.correction: The word slow has an O in it and these fibres use oxygen to contract slowly and aerobically. They are our body's first choice of muscle fibre due to fatigue resistance, hence type I.

2848.belief: Exercise is either aerobic or anaerobic and lactic acid is bad.
2848.statement: Exercise is either aerobic or anaerobic and lactic acid is bad.
2848.correction: All exercise is on a continuum from 100% aerobic (e.g. a long distance walk) to 100% anaerobic (e.g. a 1 rep max powerlifter) and the build up of lactic acid is perfectly natural and necessary to work at high intensity when insufficient O2 available.

9058.belief: The saggital plane is linked with the saggital axis.
9058.statement: The saggital plane is linked with the saggital axis.
9058.correction: They share the same name; however, the sagittal plane is linked with the frontal axis. The saggital axis is linked with the frontal plane.

9825.belief: All athletes would require large muscle mass to be successful at sport.
9825.statement: Some students may think all athletes would require large muscle mass to be successful at sport.
9825.correction: Provide a range of examples including marathon runners, sumo wrestlers to show how diverse body compositions can be advantageous in different sports.

6941.statement: Pupils may measure their heart rate incorrectly after completing the 150 steps for the Harvard step test.
6941.correction: Before starting the Harvard step test, allow pupils an opportunity to practice finding and measuring their heart rate.

7278.statement: Pupils do not stand straight against the wall with their arm touching the wall to gain the initial mark for the vertical jump test.
7278.correction: It is important for reliable results when measuring power that the arm is against the wall and outreached as high as possible, when taking the initial measurement.

903.belief: Certain sports only need one type of component of fitness to be successful, e.g. 100m sprinter just needs speed.
903.statement: Certain sports only need one type of component of fitness to be successful, e.g. 100m sprinter just needs speed.
903.correction: Identify all the components of fitness that are useful for each athlete, determining why they are beneficial and justifying which is most important.

9561.belief: Each sport/activity has only one specific type of training suited to it.
9561.statement: Each sport/activity has only one specific type of training suited to it.
9561.correction: Performers in many activities can benefit from a variety of training types. For example, a marathon runner will mostly benefit from continuous training, however weight training could help to condition their muscles and avoid injury.

3794.belief: Injuries can be prevented by using methods such as PAR-Q.
3794.statement: Injuries can be prevented by using methods such as PAR-Q
3794.correction: Nothing can guarantee that injuries will not happen, however the measures discussed in this lesson will significantly reduce the risk of injury. Accidents will always happen.

8957.belief: RICE is the treatment required for all injuries.
8957.statement: RICE is the treatment required for all injuries.
8957.correction: RICE in only suitable for soft tissue injuries such as strains and sprains. For other types of injuries, other types of medical care should be sought.

5448.belief: All performance enhancing drugs are illegal/banned/negative.
5448.statement: All performance enhancing drugs are illegal/banned/negative.
5448.correction: The use of some PEDs to enhance performance is perfectly acceptable. Many sportspeople use narcotic analgesics to get through an event or drink caffeine for its stimulating effect. WADA is responsible for determining which PEDs are allowed.

5095.belief: Once planned, I just need to take part in the training without writing anything down.
5095.statement: Once planned, I just need to take part in the training without writing anything down.
5095.correction: It is useful to keep up to date training logs for each session to help monitor progress (these are not included in the word count) as well as doing mid PEP fitness testing to check progress and adapt the planned training programme where needed.

6982.statement: Pupils often mix up what changes happen in response to exercise and what changes happen as a long term adaptation to training.
6982.correction: Short-term responses of the body are what happens as soon as we start exercising to cope with it, but if we train regularly, then the body adapts to be better able to cope with the stress of exercise and hence work more efficiently in performance.

866.belief: Cardio-respiratory benefits only come from endurance training and muscle growth only comes from weight training.
866.statement: Cardio-respiratory benefits only come from endurance training and muscle growth only comes from weight training.
866.correction: Any training that regularly puts the bodily systems under more strain than they are in normal life will lead to long term benefits to the muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems. However, training intensity will effect results.

3924.belief: All joint movements require the same sort of leverage.
3924.statement: All joint movements require the same sort of leverage.
3924.correction: The orientation of the fulcrum (joint), the effort (muscle) and the load dictate which of the three classes of lever it is and also if there is a mechanical advantage.

10271.belief: Balance is not important for games players and only useful in gymnastics.
10271.statement: Thinking that balance is not important for games players and only useful in gymnastics.
10271.correction: Provide examples of when games players would need balance, e.g. a rugby player will need balance when kicking a conversion to provide greater accuracy.

9562.belief: Each sport or activity has only one training method suited to it.
9562.statement: Each sport or activity has only one training method suited to it.
9562.correction: Perfomers in most activities can benefit from the use of multiple trianing types. For example, a marathon runner would most benefit from continuous training; however, weight training could also be used to help condition the muscles and avoid injury.

3793.belief: Injuries can be prevented in sport and physical activity.
3793.statement: Injuries can be prevented in sport and physical activity.
3793.correction: We can significantly reduce the risk of injury using the measures discussed in the lesson, however nothing can guarantee an accident causing injury to a performer.

4560.belief: Memorising and writing the definitions from the textbook earns marks.
4560.statement: Memorising and writing the definitions from the textbook earns marks.
4560.correction: Marks are only awarded for applying your knowledge to explain the implications of fitness, skill and tactical decision making on performance. With only 14 hours to complete the coursework, it is essential to focus time on application of knowledge.

7743.belief: Couch to 5k is merely to start running and be able to run 5k immediately.
7743.statement: Pupils think couch to 5k is merely to start running and be able to run 5k immediately.
7743.correction: 5k is a popular distance due to the park run (a global brand). However, couch to 5k is a beginner's approach to running using a gradual training plan, over 9 weeks from walking to running.

7929.belief: Interval training is completed to increase speed and power only.
7929.statement: Pupils think interval training is completed to increase speed and power only.
7929.correction: The rest intervals are really good to enhance stamina and cardiovascular endurance. The intense workout does develop power especially in the lower body muscles which supports injury prevention when running.

8277.belief: Squats are only limited to the gym environment.
8277.statement: Pupils think squats are only limited to the gym environment.
8277.correction: A squat is a functional whole body exercise to strengthen the lower body which can completed with weights or without (just using bodyweight as resistance), and can be completed anywhere where the space if big enough.

8285.belief: If they are struggling to achieve the guided training in the app, they have failed and have to stop.
8285.statement: Pupils think if they are struggling to achieve the guided training in the app, they have failed and have to stop.
8285.correction: The app is flexible and can be adapted to individual needs and fitness levels. Even though it is set over 9 weeks you can complete it at your own pace and revisit weeks / runs if needed.

7896.belief: Hitting your targets is the same as doing the maximum amount you can.
7896.statement: Pupils think hitting your targets is the same as doing the maximum amount you can.
7896.correction: A target needs to be SMART. It needs to be specific to the group, one you can measure, the group agrees it and it is realistic to all the abilities and fitness levels in the group. It also needs an allocated time to achieve it.

8189.belief: The race is about placing and running in the fastest time.
8189.statement: Pupils think the race is about placing and running in the fastest time.
8189.correction: Yes placings are given, but the key focus is to complete the race in a time that you know is representative of you working to the best of your ability.

7786.belief: It easier to hold the ball in 1 hand.
7786.statement: Pupils may think it easier to hold the ball in 1 hand.
7786.correction: Holding the ball in 1 hand might feel easier at first but it reduces control, increases the risk of a knock-on and makes it harder to pass accurately in both directions.

8306.belief: When they are tagged/touched, the attacker can just give the ball (1 handed) to their teammate.
8306.statement: Pupils think that when they are tagged/touched, the attacker can just give the ball (1 handed) to their teammate.
8306.correction: When tagged/touched, the attacker should present the ball with 2 hands and their teammate should rip the ball with 2 hands to keep it safe and avoid fumbles and knock ons.

8307.belief: Just the tagger remains at the breakdown in T1 rugby.
8307.statement: Pupils think that just the tagger remains at the breakdown in T1 rugby.
8307.correction: After a tag/touch, 2 other defenders need to join the the tager to form a triangle at every breakdown.

8233.belief: A scrum and line out in T1 rugby are contested and they push to get the ball.
8233.statement: Pupils think a scrum and line out in T1 rugby are contested and they push to get the ball.
8233.correction: T1 rugby is a non contact game therefore the scrum and lineouts are both uncontested. They are used to draw players into an area to create space on the pitch following a restart.

7661.belief: It is always best to pass when in a difficult situation.
7661.statement: Pupils think that it is always best to pass when in a difficult situation.
7661.correction: Retaining possession through accurate kicks can at times make more yards than passing and being tagged.

8114.belief: Performance is only determined by how many tries you scored.
8114.statement: Pupils think that performance is only determined by how many tries you scored.
8114.correction: A player can have a strong impact without getting a try by helping their team keep possession, organise defence or create space for others.

6680.statement: Pupils forget that after 2 goals are scored they swap positions.
6680.correction: After 2 goals are scored in Korfball, the attackers then swap and become the defenders and the defenders swap and become attackers (on both teams).

7588.belief: They only have 3 seconds to pass the ball like in netball.
7588.statement: Pupils think they only have 3 seconds to pass the ball like in netball.
7588.correction: In Korfball pupils have 4 seconds to pass the ball.

4635.belief: Misconception: Pupils think you should always use two hands to shoot in Korfball.
4635.statement: Misconception: Pupils think you should always use two hands to shoot in Korfball.
4635.correction: Two-handed shots are useful, especially when you're learning, but they’re not always the best choice. In a match, you might need to shoot quickly or when a defender is close. One-handed shots can be faster and harder to block.

7951.belief: Korfball is a contact sport where you can push players.
7951.statement: Pupils think that Korfball is a contact sport where you can push players.
7951.correction: Korfball allows incidental contact that is natural movement, e.g. brushing shoulders and close marking, however pushing, holding or blocking is not allowed.

7757.belief: It is only defenders that screen attackers.
7757.statement: Pupils think it is only defenders that screen attackers.
7757.correction: Attackers should also screen defenders to allow other attacking teammates to run into the space.

7948.belief: A knock out tournament is always the best type of tournament to do in sport/ PE.
7948.statement: Pupils think that a knock out tournament is always the best type of tournament to do in sport/ PE.
7948.correction: With 4 or less teams (or if you have a lot of time) a round-robin tournament is better so that all teams are able to play each other.

3620.belief: I'm not flexible so I can't do yoga.
3620.statement: I'm not flexible so I can't do yoga.
3620.correction: Flexibility develops over time with consistent practice. Yoga also improves strength, balance and mindfulness. Many poses can be modified to suit all levels, so anyone can start, no matter their current flexibility.

3517.belief: Holding your breath when performing different moves or going deeper into a stretch is beneficial.
3517.statement: Holding your breath when performing different moves or going deeper into a stretch is beneficial.
3517.correction: Holding your breath while performing movements or deepening a stretch can create tension, reduce oxygen flow and limit flexibility. Focus on steady, controlled breathing to help the body relax, move safely and maximise the benefits of each pose.

5520.belief: Pilates is easy and only develops flexibility.
5520.statement: Pilates is easy and only develops flexibility.
5520.correction: Pilates builds core strength, stability and muscular endurance, and can be challenging for all types of athletes. It’s not just stretching, it’s a full-body workout that improves posture, balance and overall strength.

8409.belief: Yoga is always slow and steady, and is only for relaxation.
8409.statement: Pupils think that yoga is always slow and steady, and is only for relaxation.
8409.correction: Yoga can be both calming and energising, depending on the style and intention of the practice.

8212.statement: Pupils think that resistance bands make exercises easier
8212.correction: Resistance bands actually add extra tension, making movements more challenging. They engage muscles throughout the entire movement, improving strength, control and stability more effectively than bodyweight exercises alone.

8408.statement: Pupils think yin yoga is boring.
8408.correction: Yin Yoga provides a chance to deeply connect with your body and mind. It can be a deeply meditative practice, allowing for self-reflection and stress relief. For many, it’s an opportunity to slow down in an otherwise fast-paced life.

8459.statement: Pupils will often tuck their thumbs under fingers or stick them out.
8459.correction: Pupils should lock thumbs around the outside of their fist to adopt the correct guard stance.

6781.statement: Pupils hold the pads at the wrong height or angle or keep their arms too stiff or too relaxed.
6781.correction: Encourage pupils to communicate if the pads are at the wrong height or angle to give each other corrective feedback. Teach pad holders to “meet” the strike with slight forward pressure and a bend in the arms.

6398.statement: Pupils often drop their guard after blocking leaving their head and body exposed.
6398.correction: Focus on returning to the guard stance after every block and continue to prompt pupils throughout the lesson.

7283.statement: Pupils often start exercises with too much intensity and quickly recognise that they cannot continue when performing conditioning exercises.
7283.correction: When trying to improve muscular endurance and condition, steady and continuous activity over a longer period of time gives the best results. Start at a pace that is comfortable to begin with and can be maintained as muscles start to fatigue.

7075.statement: Pupils perform movements too fast or too slow which disrupts the flow of the kata.
7075.correction: Performing Chon-Ji at a consistent tempo and speed helps to develop cardiovascular and muscular endurance. It enhances mental focus and breath control. The different speeds simulate real combat situations which will vary in speed and acceleration.

8237.statement: Pupils think that self-defence is just like fighting.
8237.correction: Self-defence focuses on escape and de-escalation. It is about avoiding harm and getting away safely.

2166.belief: Dance styles are set and never change.
2166.statement: Dance styles are set and never change.
2166.correction: Dance styles continually evolve. When studying dances from history or other places, we are able to pinpoint key attributes that were relevant at a point in time, they may remain or they may be adapted.

2063.correction: Counterbalances can involve the same action as a partner but these can be varied by level, direction of size. Counterbalances can also use contrasting body parts to connect, e.g. the hand of one dancer pressing against the shoulder of their partner.

2157.belief: Dance actions should always be performed as big as possible so they are clear and stand out to an audience.
2157.statement: Dance actions should always be performed as big as possible so they are clear and stand out to an audience.
2157.correction: Whilst this is often the case for performance dances, social dances are often much smaller and more relaxed in their execution since they are often performed in a limited amount of space and purely for pleasure, rather than an audience.

9062.belief: In Salsa you have to apply tension to your whole body.
9062.statement: In Salsa you have to apply tension to your whole body.
9062.correction: In Salsa it is the torso that is firmly held maintaining an upright stance, the arms are also fixed when in hold but change to some degree when moving between holds or when moving independently. The legs largely remain soft and fluid.

2977.belief: Films made for entertainment are an accurate representation of a social dance style.
2977.statement: Films made for entertainment are an accurate representation of a social dance style.
2977.correction: Whilst many choreographers may have researched a social dance and employed the key features, it is unlikely that it is a detailed and accurate representation, and should be considered to be 'in the style of' rather than an authentic account.

5455.belief: Performers have to smile all the time.
5455.statement: Performers have to smile all the time.
5455.correction: Performers use facial expression to communicate the mood or feelings of their character. This range can include smiling if happy, weeping if sad, a furrowed brow if worried, a cleanched jaw if angry or eye-rolling if annoyed.

8035.belief: They need to hit the ball hard to slice effectively.
8035.statement: Pupils think they need to hit the ball hard to slice effectively.
8035.correction: Pushing and slicing require a light touch and controlled movements, not power.

7893.belief: They should hit the ball with a flat racket face to generate topspin.
7893.statement: Pupils think they should hit the ball with a flat racket face to generate topspin.
7893.correction: To create topspin, you need to angle the racket slightly downward and brush up the back of the ball.

6169.belief: They can just win by hitting the ball with power.
6169.statement: Pupils believe they can just win by hitting the ball with power.
6169.correction: Winning in table tennis isn’t just about power as control, spin, placement and consistency are just as important. A well-placed shot forces your opponent into difficult returns and increases your accuracy in rallies.

7754.belief: Deception is only about tricking your opponent with flashy shots (e.g. through the legs).
7754.statement: Pupils think that deception is only about tricking your opponent with flashy shots (e.g. through the legs).
7754.correction: Effective deception is about subtle changes in timing, swing and shot placement. It doesn’t always require exaggerated fakes - small delays or slight adjustments can be just as effective in disrupting your opponent’s rhythm.

2483.belief: In doubles, players should stand on the left and right and just hit the ball on their side (like tennis or badminton).
2483.statement: In doubles, players should stand on the left and right and just hit the ball on their side (like tennis or badminton).
2483.correction: In doubles in table tennis, players have to hit alternate shots which means once you have hit the ball, you need to move out of the way so your partner can hit the next shot. Just standing on sides will make it difficult to play alternate shots.

7862.belief: In a game you should always try hit the ball to the back of the table to win.
7862.statement: Pupils think that in a game you should always try hit the ball to the back of the table to win.
7862.correction: While hitting to the back of the table can be effective, it's not always the best strategy. Mixing up your shots, using different spins and placing the ball in various spots on the table can be more effective.

3508.belief: To hit the ball in golf, you lift your head up to look at the target.
3508.statement: To hit the ball in golf, you lift your head up to look at the target.
3508.correction: Explain to pupils that in order to hit the ball successfully you need to keep your head down and focused on the ball.

8185.belief: You can putt the ball successfully just by lining up to the ball, forgetting that the green slopes and isn't flat.
8185.statement: Pupils think you can putt the ball successfully just by lining up to the ball, forgetting that the green slopes and isn't flat.
8185.correction: Explain to pupils that beacuse each green is different and they aren't flat, we always have to consider where we aim and the power we apply.

7868.belief: We only get a penalty stroke if we break a rule.
7868.statement: Pupils think we only get a penalty stroke if we break a rule.
7868.correction: Explain to pupils that a a penalty stroke is an extra stroke added to your score as a result of breaking a rule or hitting the ball into certain areas.

3331.belief: Golf etiquette is just about being polite.
3331.statement: Golf etiquette is just about being polite.
3331.correction: Explain to pupils that golf etiquette is about courtesy, consideration and respect for other players, the course and the game itself.

10314.belief: Throwing the baton harder increases success.
10314.statement: Throwing the baton harder increases success.
10314.correction: Kubb is a game of accuracy and control, replicating the same technique will increase accuracy and consistency with practice.

2847.belief: Exclusive focus on winning limits satisfaction and enjoyment.
2847.statement: Exclusive focus on winning limits satisfaction and enjoyment.
2847.correction: Games like Kubb should be as much about the enjoyable social experience and finding ways to support each other as well as demonstrating honesty and fair play as winning the match.

9364.correction: They are not interchangeable. Skill is learnt and developed through practice, while ability is a natural and inherited trait often considered innate. An ability provides an opportunity or the potential to develop a skill.

1803.belief: A very common mistake made when classifying skills is to name a sport without the skill. For example, trying to classify 'rugby' rather than one of the many different skills within rugby.
1803.statement: A very common mistake made when classifying skills is to name a sport without the skill. For example, trying to classify 'rugby' rather than one of the many different skills within rugby.
1803.correction: Ensure pupils understand that specific skills are required and that they can name multiple examples of skills from different sports.

9365.belief: Skills must be one classification or the other, e.g., a skill is either gross or fine.
9365.statement: Skills must be one classification or the other, e.g., a skill is either gross or fine.
9365.correction: Ensure pupils understand a continua allows for skills to be classified anywhere along it, and that some skills may fall somewhere between two different classifications.

1815.belief: It is common to see variants on the SMART acronym, for example, R = realistic, from other exam boards or sources. Some sources may extend the acronym to SMARTER.
1815.statement: It is common to see variants on the SMART acronym, for example, R = realistic, from other exam boards or sources. Some sources may extend the acronym to SMARTER.
1815.correction: Ensure it is understood that with the OCR exam board, SMART only ever refers to Specific, Measurable, Achieveable, Recorded and Timed.

3801.belief: The input part of the model is largely based on being able to use sight to inform the brain.
3801.statement: The input part of the model is largely based on being able to use sight to inform the brain.
3801.correction: Input is gathering data from all the senses. In sport, these can be what you see, hear, feel and touch.

6108.belief: Only one type of guidance can be used at any time.
6108.statement: Pupils may believe that only one type of guidance can be used at any time.
6108.correction: Combinations of guidance can be very effective and are common in good coaching. For example, visual demonstrations are often combined with verbal explanations.

10499.belief: Types of feedback are often confused with types of guidance from the previous lesson.
10499.statement: Types of feedback are often confused with types of guidance from the previous lesson.
10499.correction: Ensure students can differentiate between guidance being information needed to understand how to perform a skill, and feedback being information about how well it is being performed.

383.belief: The more arousal you have, the better you perform.
383.statement: The more arousal you have, the better you perform.
383.correction: The inverted-U theory recognises that after an optimal level of arousal, performance will deteriorate with any further heightening of arousal levels.

4569.belief: Mental preparation is just for elite athletes.
4569.statement: Mental preparation is just for elite athletes.
4569.correction: Students should understand that everyone can benefit from mental preparation techniques and that performers in many fields of work practice them. They too could benefit in their own pursuits.

85.belief: All acts of aggression involve violence and are the result of anger.
85.statement: All acts of aggression involve violence and are the result of anger.
85.correction: Some aggressive acts are controlled and are used to gain a performance advantage in sport. They are also within the rules of sports such as rugby and combat sports.

4105.belief: This lesson gives the impression that there are only two types of people and people should be defined as one or the other personality.
4105.statement: This lesson gives the impression that there are only two types of people and people should be defined as one or the other personality.
4105.correction: Although the AQA specification has clear definitions of how introverts and extroverts typically behave, which will be required knowledge in the exam, students should understand that people's personality is more nuanced and goes beyond these.

3845.belief: Intrinsic motivation is always the best type of motivation.
3845.statement: Intrinsic motivation is always the best type of motivation.
3845.correction: Extrinsic motivation has its time and place, particularly with short term goals or with very young people. Intrinsic is much better when long term commitment and persistence is required.

609.belief: Certain sports or activities are only suitable for certain types of people. For example, girls don't play rugby.
609.statement: Believing that certain sports or activities are only suitable for certain types of people. For example, girls don't play rugby.
609.correction: Some people face barriers in accessing sport or physical activity, however, these barriers should be broken down to provide opportunities for everyone to access all sport and physical activities.

614.belief: Only one factor can affect participation such as gender, when actually there are lots of factors that can affect participation in physical activity.
614.statement: Believing that only one factor can affect participation such as gender, when actually there are lots of factors that can affect participation in physical activity.
614.correction: Some people may not face any barriers to participation, however some people may experience a number of different factors that affect whether they participate in a sport or not.

5172.belief: Only one value can be shown on a graph.
5172.statement: Only one value can be shown on a graph.
5172.correction: Different values can be broken down into different categories, such as the age of people and their participation in different activities, which gives a more detailed picture of participants.

7994.belief: Media coverage is always beneficial for sports, without considering potential negative effects and assuming that media only affects athletes and fans.
7994.statement: Pupils may think that media coverage is always beneficial for sports, without considering potential negative effects and assuming that media only affects athletes and fans.
7994.correction: Media coverage can be both positive and negative and can impact performers, sports, officials, spectators and the sport itself.

9946.belief: Sport only benefits from media and sponsorship.
9946.statement: Students might think that sport only benefits from media and sponsorship.
9946.correction: Media and sponsorship also benefit from the sport.

617.statement: Believing that sponsorship only involves financial support.
617.correction: Sponsorship can include financial support but also include equipment, clothing or facility provisions.

619.belief: Technology always improves performance without considering potential drawbacks.
619.statement: Believing that technology always improves performance without considering potential drawbacks.
619.correction: Technology has both positive and negative impacts on different people in sport, including performers, sponsors, spectators and officials.

6810.statement: Pupils may incorrectly assume that sportsmanship and gamemanship are the same thing.
6810.correction: Sportsmanship is positively conforming to the rules and etiquette of the sport, whereas gamesmanship is more negative because a performer may bend the rules to gain advantage.

5379.belief: All PEDs are automatically illegal and banned substances.
5379.statement: All PEDs are automatically illegal and banned substances.
5379.correction: Not all are instantly illegal or banned. For example, some stimulants are legal such as caffeine which is used by many as a stimulant. Beta blockers are available on prescription and therefore have certain restrictions.

616.belief: Spectators always have a negative effect on performance and safety and the impact of spectators is only relevant in professional sport.
616.statement: Believing that spectators always have a negative effect on performance and safety and the impact of spectators is only relevant in professional sport.
616.correction: Spectators have positive contributions to sport like creating an atmosphere and providing home-field advantage which can not only affect professional sport, but also amateur and youth sport too.

9774.statement: Students might mistakenly believe hooliganism is limited to football.
9774.correction: Hooliganism can happen in other sports and activities but is it most widely known in football.

6286.statement: Pupils can often confuse the x and y axis and therefore not read the correct x axis information.
6286.correction: On a bar or line graphs pupils should get into the habit of physically going along the bottom to read the information along the x axis.

9914.belief: Being physically fit means they are automatically healthy.
9914.statement: Students think that being physically fit means they are automatically healthy.
9914.correction: Explain the importance of social and emotional benefits too, particularly for participants such as elderly people.

615.belief: A sedentary lifestyle only affects physical health through weight gain.
615.statement: Believing that a sedentary lifestyle only affects physical health through weight gain.
615.correction: A sedentary lifestyle can have a negative impact on social and emotional health too.

612.belief: Individuals fit exclusively into one somatotype category rather than having a mix of characteristics.
612.statement: Believing that individuals fit exclusively into one somatotype category rather than having a mix of characteristics.
612.correction: Individuals can have a mix of characteristics from different somatotypes but can also change their somatotype depending on their lifestyle choices.

2849.belief: "If I did more exercise, I'd lose weight".
2849.statement: "If I did more exercise, I'd lose weight"
2849.correction: While exercise will increase energy expenditure and could help to achieve a calorie deficit needed to lose weight, "you can't out train a bad diet." No matter how much exercise is performed, calorie intake is just as important to consider.

4418.belief: There are many misconceptions about diet, such as the need to cut out carbohydrates or fat because they are seen as responsible for weight gain.
4418.statement: There are many misconceptions about diet, such as the need to cut out carbohydrates or fat because they are seen as responsible for weight gain.
4418.correction: A balanced diet requires all nutrients because each has its own benefits to the body and health. Cutting any of them out completely will negatively impact overall health and performance in sport and physical activity.

4351.belief: The main consequences of dehydration are headaches and dizziness.
4351.statement: The main consequences of dehydration are headaches and dizziness.
4351.correction: Headaches and dizziness are likely effects of dehydration, however the GCSE specification expects students to be able to understand the physiological reasons behind these such as slow blood flow, increased heart rate and body temperature.

46.belief: For a 6 mark answer, I have to make one knowledge point, two applications and three AO3's.
46.statement: For a 6 mark answer, I have to make one knowledge point, two applications and three AO3's.
46.correction: 6 mark answers are marked holistically using a levelled response grid. Level descriptors are applied to the overall response. A quantative approach to answering these questions can be limiting to develop the breadth of knowledge and depth of AO3.

48.belief: For a 9 mark answer, I have to make two knowledge points, two applications and five AO3s.
48.statement: For a 9 mark answer, I have to make two knowledge points, two applications and five AO3s.
48.correction: 9 mark answers are marked holistically using a levelled response grid. Level descriptors are applied to the overall response. A quantitative approach to answering these questions can be limiting to develop the breadth of knowledge and depth of AO3.

607.belief: It might be believed that certain sports only require one type of practice structure.
607.statement: It might be believed that certain sports only require one type of practice structure.
607.correction: Practice structures vary depending on the skills being practiced and the level of ability. Two different skills from within the same sport might benefit from different practice structures.

9763.statement: Students may incorrectly assume that sportsmanship and gamemanship are the same thing.
9763.correction: Sportsmanship is positively conforming to the rules and etiquette of the sport, whereas gamesmanship is more negative because a performer may bend the rules to gain advantage.

9832.belief: The only benefits to exercise are physical benefits.
9832.statement: Students think the only benefits to exercise are physical benefits.
9832.correction: Explain the importance of social and emotional benefits too, particularly for participants such as elderly people.

9994.statement: Students may view lifestyle choices as something that can only be negative (e.g. fatty food, sedentary lifestyle or drugs).
9994.correction: Reframe thinking using positive examples of each factor.

5475.belief: Personal exercise programmes are only used by people that play sport.
5475.statement: Personal exercise programmes are only used by people that play sport.
5475.correction: Perosnal exercise programmes can be used by everyone to increase physical activity levels.

4256.belief: In long answer questions, it is better to recall as much of the topic as possible.
4256.statement: In long answer questions, it is better to recall as much of the topic as possible.
4256.correction: It is important to recall the specific knowledge relevant to the question, but then you must apply and develop that knowledge based on the command word. Simply recalling knowledge will only hit AO1 marks awarded.

5452.belief: Performance in sport is entirely down to physiological capabilities such as speed, strength and technique.
5452.statement: Performance in sport is entirely down to physiological capabilities such as speed, strength and technique.
5452.correction: Psychological factors such as confidence, motivation and learned behaviours from similar experiences in the past, have as much impact on performance in sport, as the level of skill that players have.

5903.belief: Provision only includes funding or money.
5903.statement: Provision only includes funding or money.
5903.correction: Increasing provision can also include improving facilities, time, coaching and equipment.

4943.belief: NGBs only support elite sports people at the top of their game.
4943.statement: NGBs only support elite sports people at the top of their game.
4943.correction: NGBs provide support to everyone, from grass roots level all the way up to elite level sport.

2909.belief: Failure to address all parts of the question.
2909.statement: Failure to address all parts of the question.
2909.correction: The 6 mark extended answer question always requires knowledge from that exam paper (component) and the other exam paper (component) and practical application.
